      # PRD: Project Scheduling Application for Development Teams
      
      **Status:** Draft 0.1 | **Owner:** (TBD) | **Date:** October 9, 2026
      
      > This draft is based on an initial feature description. Anything not yet known is written as an **assumption** (marked [A]) or an **open question** (section 14) so it can be validated before development begins.
      
      ## 1. Summary
      
      An application for building, calculating, and visualizing software project schedules. Users create a project, structure tasks hierarchically with dependencies, set up working calendars and team member leave, and then view the result as a Gantt Chart, a PERT/Network Diagram, and a critical path. The system automatically calculates task dates from durations, dependencies, and calendars.
      
      ## 2. Background and Problem Statement
      
      Project managers and tech leads of development teams struggle to build and track realistic schedules because task dependencies, holidays, and team availability must be calculated manually (usually in spreadsheets). As a result, schedules are error-prone, hard to update when things change, and delay risk (the critical path) stays invisible.
      
      **Supporting evidence:** none yet. Needs to be gathered through interviews with 5-8 PMs/tech leads and samples of the schedules they use today (see section 14).
      
      ## 3. Goals and Non-Goals
      
      ### Goals
      1. Speed up creation of an initial project schedule compared with manual methods.
      2. Produce correct task dates automatically from dependencies and calendars.
      3. Make the critical path clearly visible so delay risks can be anticipated.
      4. Provide a visual overview of the schedule (Gantt and PERT) that is easy to share.
      
      ### Non-Goals (first version)
      - Project cost/budget calculation from salaries.
      - Automatic resource leveling.
      - Real-time multi-user collaboration.
      - Time tracking and timesheets.
      - Third-party integrations (Jira, Slack, etc.).
      
      ## 4. Users and Scenarios
      
      | Persona | Description | Key needs |
      |---|---|---|
      | **Project Manager / Tech Lead** (primary) | Builds and maintains software project schedules | Build schedules quickly, see the impact of changes, find the critical path |
      | **Team member** [A] | Task recipient | View their tasks and schedule (read-only in v1) |
      | **Stakeholder** [A] | Management/client | View a schedule summary via export |
      
      **Primary scenario:** A PM creates a new project, sets the working calendar, enters tasks and sub-tasks, links them with dependencies, assigns team members, then opens the Gantt chart and critical path to check whether the deadline is achievable. When a task slips or a member goes on leave, the PM changes the data and sees the schedule recalculated.
      
      ## 5. Success Metrics
      
      | Metric | Baseline | Target (proposed) |
      |---|---|---|
      | Time to build an initial schedule for a 50-task project | Measure current method | At least 50% reduction |
      | Correctness of date and critical path calculations | - | 100% pass on reference test cases |
      | Users who build a complete schedule (project with tasks, dependencies, assignments) within the first 7 days | - | 40% |
      | Projects whose schedule is updated more than once | - | 50% |
      | User satisfaction (SUS or short survey) | - | Score of 70 or higher |
      
      Baselines and targets need to be validated with the product owner.
      
      ## 6. Scope
      
      **In scope (MVP):** all modules in section 7, with FS and SS dependencies, one calendar per project, per-member leave calendars, Gantt, PERT, and critical path.
      
      **Deferred:** cost from salaries, FF/SF, resource leveling, advanced baseline and progress tracking, notifications, real-time collaboration, MS Project import, mobile app.
      
      ## 7. Functional Requirements
      
      Priority: **P0** required for MVP, **P1** should have, **P2** later.
      
      ### 7.1 Project Management
      
      | ID | Requirement | Priority |
      |---|---|---|
      | PRJ-1 | Users can create a project with a **name** (required), **organization**, and **description**. | P0 |
      | PRJ-2 | Users can view the project list, open, edit, and delete projects (with confirmation). | P0 |
      | PRJ-3 | Users can duplicate a project as a template. | P2 |
      
      **Acceptance criteria for PRJ-1:** an empty name is rejected with a clear message; the project is saved and appears in the list; a default calendar is created automatically.
      
      ### 7.2 Working Calendar
      
      | ID | Requirement | Priority |
      |---|---|---|
      | CAL-1 | Users define the **working days** per week and working hours per day [A: default Monday-Friday, 8 hours]. | P0 |
      | CAL-2 | Users define **weekend** days that are excluded from calculations. | P0 |
      | CAL-3 | Users add, edit, and delete **custom/national holidays** (date, name, optional date range). | P0 |
      | CAL-4 | Import the Indonesian national holiday list as a template. | P1 |
      | CAL-5 | Any calendar change triggers recalculation of the whole schedule. | P0 |
      
      **Acceptance criteria for CAL-5:** after adding a holiday in the middle of a task's range, the task's end date shifts accordingly and successor tasks shift with it.
      
      ### 7.3 Task Management
      
      | ID | Requirement | Priority |
      |---|---|---|
      | TSK-1 | Users add tasks with a **name**, **start date**, **duration** (working days), and **priority** (Low/Medium/High/Critical). | P0 |
      | TSK-2 | Users edit, delete, and reorder tasks. | P0 |
      | TSK-3 | **Sub-activities:** tasks can be nested under a parent task (hierarchy up to [A] 4 levels). | P0 |
      | TSK-4 | Parent tasks are calculated automatically from their children (earliest start to latest finish); parent duration is not entered manually. | P0 |
      | TSK-5 | **Milestone** task type (duration 0). | P1 |
      | TSK-6 | Additional fields: description, percent complete. | P1 |
      | TSK-7 | Indent/outdent to change task level, and copy/paste tasks. | P1 |
      
      **Acceptance criteria for TSK-1:** duration must be a positive number; a start date falling on a non-working day is automatically moved to the next working day; the end date is calculated from duration and calendar.
      
      ### 7.4 Task Dependencies
      
      | ID | Requirement | Priority |
      |---|---|---|
      | DEP-1 | Users set one or more **predecessors** on a task. | P0 |
      | DEP-2 | **Finish-to-Start (FS)**: the task starts after its predecessor finishes. | P0 |
      | DEP-3 | **Start-to-Start (SS)**: the task starts together with or after its predecessor starts. | P0 |
      | DEP-4 | **Delay/lag** in working days between tasks (negative lag/lead allowed [A]). | P0 |
      | DEP-5 | The system **prevents circular dependencies** and shows a message identifying the cycle. | P0 |
      | DEP-6 | When a task has several predecessors, its start date is taken from the latest constraint. | P0 |
      | DEP-7 | FF and SF types. | P2 |
      
      **Acceptance criteria for DEP-2/4:** task B with predecessor A (FS, 2-day delay) starts 2 working days after A finishes, taking holidays into account.
      
      ### 7.5 Resource Management
      
      | ID | Requirement | Priority |
      |---|---|---|
      | RES-1 | Users record team members: **name**, **contact** (email/phone), **role/position**, and **salary**. | P0 |
      | RES-2 | Users edit and delete members (a warning is shown if the member still has assignments). | P0 |
      | RES-3 | Users set personal **leave/days off** (date range, note) per member. | P0 |
      | RES-4 | **Salary** data is visible only to authorized users and stored encrypted. In the MVP salary is only stored, not used to compute cost. | P0 |
      | RES-5 | Users can hide the salary field from views and exports. | P1 |
      
      ### 7.6 Task Assignment
      
      | ID | Requirement | Priority |
      |---|---|---|
      | ASN-1 | Users assign **one or more** members to a task. | P0 |
      | ASN-2 | Tasks show assigned member names in the list and on the Gantt bar. | P0 |
      | ASN-3 | The system **warns** if an assigned member is on leave during the task or has other overlapping tasks. | P1 |
      | ASN-4 | Member leave affects task dates (per-resource calendar) [A: in the MVP a warning is enough; scheduling with resource calendars is P2]. | P2 |
      | ASN-5 | Filter the schedule and tasks by member. | P1 |
      
      ### 7.7 Visualization
      
      **Gantt Chart**
      
      | ID | Requirement | Priority |
      |---|---|---|
      | GNT-1 | Task list on the left and bars on a calendar timeline on the right. | P0 |
      | GNT-2 | Dependency arrows between bars; holidays and weekends shaded. | P0 |
      | GNT-3 | Timeline zoom (day, week, month). | P0 |
      | GNT-4 | Distinct shapes for parent tasks and milestones; a "today" line. | P1 |
      | GNT-5 | Change dates/duration by dragging bars; create dependencies by drawing lines. | P1 |
      | GNT-6 | Export to image or PDF. | P1 |
      
      **PERT Chart / Network Diagram**
      
      | ID | Requirement | Priority |
      |---|---|---|
      | PRT-1 | Show tasks as nodes connected by dependency arrows, automatically laid out left to right. | P0 |
      | PRT-2 | Nodes show name, duration, start and end dates (optional: ES/EF/LS/LF and slack). | P0 |
      | PRT-3 | Pan, zoom, and click a node to see task details. | P0 |
      | PRT-4 | Export to image or PDF. | P1 |
      
      ### 7.8 Critical Path Analysis
      
      | ID | Requirement | Priority |
      |---|---|---|
      | CPM-1 | The system calculates the critical path using the Critical Path Method (forward and backward pass) based on durations, dependencies, and calendars. | P0 |
      | CPM-2 | Critical tasks (slack = 0) are highlighted in the Gantt, PERT, and task list. | P0 |
      | CPM-3 | Show **slack/float** per task. | P1 |
      | CPM-4 | Show the project end date and total project duration. | P0 |
      | CPM-5 | Support more than one critical path when present. | P1 |
      | CPM-6 | Highlighting updates automatically whenever data changes. | P0 |
      
      **Acceptance criteria for CPM-1:** results match reference test cases (at least 5 task networks calculated by hand, including SS, lag, and holiday cases).
      
      ## 8. Scheduling Rules
      
      1. Duration is counted in **working days**; non-working days and holidays are skipped.
      2. Task start date = the maximum of (user-entered start date, the constraint set by all predecessors after lag).
      3. Task end date = start date plus working-day duration minus one.
      4. Parent task: start = earliest child start, end = latest child end.
      5. Dependencies to or from a parent task are treated at the parent level [A].
      6. Any change triggers recalculation of the whole task graph (target: under 1 second for 500 tasks).
      7. Data must never be saved in a state with a dependency cycle.
      
      ## 9. Non-Functional Requirements
      
      - **Performance:** recalculation and Gantt rendering for 500 tasks in under 1 second; support up to 2,000 tasks per project.
      - **Security and privacy:** salary and contact data are personal data; role-based access, encryption at rest and in transit, compliance with Indonesia's Personal Data Protection Law (UU PDP) if cloud storage is used.
      - **Reliability:** autosave; no data loss when the browser is closed.
      - **Usability:** Indonesian and English interface [A]; keyboard-friendly for fast task entry.
      - **Compatibility:** latest modern browsers (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari) [A: web-based].
      - **Accessibility:** adequate color contrast; the critical path is not distinguished by color alone (add icon/thickness).
      - **Testing:** the scheduling engine has automated tests with reference cases.
      
      ## 10. Data Model (Outline)
      
      - **Project:** id, name, organization, description, calendar id.
      - **Calendar:** working days, working hours per day, list of holidays (date, name).
      - **Task:** id, project id, parent id, order, name, description, start date (input), duration, priority, percent complete; computed: effective start/end, slack, critical flag.
      - **Dependency:** predecessor id, successor id, type (FS/SS), lag.
      - **Resource:** id, name, contact, role, salary.
      - **ResourceLeave:** resource id, start date, end date, note.
      - **Assignment:** task id, resource id.
      
      ## 11. Main User Flow
      
      1. Create a project, then set the working calendar and holidays.
      2. Add team members and their leave.
      3. Build tasks and sub-tasks with durations and priorities.
      4. Link tasks with predecessors, types, and lag.
      5. Assign members to tasks.
      6. Open the Gantt, PERT, and critical path highlighting; check the project end date.
      7. Change data as things shift and see the impact; export to share.
      
      ## 12. Assumptions, Risks, and Dependencies
      
      | Risk / Assumption | Impact | Mitigation |
      |---|---|---|
      | The scheduling engine (calendars, FS/SS, lag, hierarchy) is complex and bug-prone | Wrong schedules, loss of user trust | Isolate the module, reference test cases, early technical spike |
      | Automatic PERT layout is hard to read for large networks | Cluttered diagrams | Use a mature graph library, provide zoom and filters |
      | Salary data is sensitive | Leaks and compliance issues | Restricted access, encryption, option to omit salary |
      | Scope resembles full MS Project | Scope creep | Hold the MVP boundary, review feature requests each release |
      | Users are used to Excel/MS Project | Low adoption | Import/export, short onboarding, project templates |
      | Product differentiator is unclear | Hard to compete | Decide positioning (section 13) |
      
      ## 13. Competitive Landscape and Differentiation
      
      **Alternatives:** Microsoft Project, ProjectLibre, GanttProject, OpenProject, TeamGantt, Smartsheet, Jira Advanced Roadmaps, and Excel.
      
      **Differentiators the product owner needs to choose from:** (a) simpler and faster to learn, (b) free or cheap for small teams, (c) focused on software development teams, (d) local data/privacy, (e) another angle. This decision affects feature priorities and the interface.
      
      ## 14. Open Questions
      
      1. Who is the primary user, and how large are the teams/projects targeted?
      2. Platform: web, desktop, or both? Single user or multi-user with login?
      3. Is data stored locally or in the cloud? Are access roles (admin, PM, member) needed?
      4. What is salary data used for? If for project cost, does the cost feature go in the MVP or a later phase?
      5. Should member leave change task dates, or is a warning enough?
      6. Are FF/SF dependency types and lead (negative lag) needed?
      7. Duration unit: working days only, or hours too?
      8. Is progress tracking and baseline vs. actual needed?
      9. Is import/export needed (Excel, MS Project, PDF, image)?
      10. What is the main product differentiator, and who is the main competitor?
      11. What are the release deadline, budget, and development team composition?
      
      ## 15. Proposed Release Phases
      
      | Phase | Contents | Outcome |
      |---|---|---|
      | **0. Discovery** | User interviews, resolve open questions, scheduling engine spike | Final PRD and technical decisions |
      | **1. Core MVP** | Projects, calendar, tasks and sub-tasks, FS/SS dependencies and lag, schedule calculation | Schedules can be calculated and tested |
      | **2. Full MVP** | Resources, leave, assignments, Gantt, PERT, critical path | Pilot release to early users |
      | **3. Refinement** | Drag and drop, export, workload warnings, slack | Public release |
      | **4. Advanced** | Cost from salaries, progress and baseline, MS Project import, collaboration | Based on feedback |
      
      ## 16. Approvals
      
      | Role | Name | Status |
      |---|---|---|
      | Product owner | | Pending |
      | Engineering | | Pending |
      | Design | | Pending |
      | Data/Security (salary data) | | Pending |

      ## About Laravel
      
      Laravel is a web application framework with expressive, elegant syntax. We believe development must be an enjoyable and creative experience to be truly fulfilling. Laravel takes the pain out of development by easing common tasks used in many web projects, such as:
      
      - [Simple, fast routing engine](https://laravel.com/docs/routing).
      - [Powerful dependency injection container](https://laravel.com/docs/container).
      - Multiple back-ends for [session](https://laravel.com/docs/session) and [cache](https://laravel.com/docs/cache) storage.
      - Expressive, intuitive [database ORM](https://laravel.com/docs/eloquent).
      - Database agnostic [schema migrations](https://laravel.com/docs/migrations).
      - [Robust background job processing](https://laravel.com/docs/queues).
      - [Real-time event broadcasting](https://laravel.com/docs/broadcasting).
      
      Laravel is accessible, powerful, and provides tools required for large, robust applications.
      
      ## Learning Laravel
      
      Laravel has the most extensive and thorough [documentation](https://laravel.com/docs) and video tutorial library of all modern web application frameworks, making it a breeze to get started with the framework.
      
      In addition, [Laracasts](https://laracasts.com) contains thousands of video tutorials on a range of topics including Laravel, modern PHP, unit testing, and JavaScript. Boost your skills by digging into our comprehensive video library.
      
      You can also watch bite-sized lessons with real-world projects on [Laravel Learn](https://laravel.com/learn), where you will be guided through building a Laravel application from scratch while learning PHP fundamentals.
      
      ## Agentic Development
      
      Laravel's predictable structure and conventions make it ideal for AI coding agents like Claude Code, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot. Install [Laravel Boost](https://laravel.com/docs/ai) to supercharge your AI workflow:
      
      ```bash
      composer require laravel/boost --dev
      
      php artisan boost:install
      ```
      
      Boost provides your agent 15+ tools and skills that help agents build Laravel applications while following best practices.
      
      ## Contributing
      
      Thank you for considering contributing to the Laravel framework! The contribution guide can be found in the [Laravel documentation](https://laravel.com/docs/contributions).
      
      ## Code of Conduct
      
      In order to ensure that the Laravel community is welcoming to all, please review and abide by the [Code of Conduct](https://laravel.com/docs/contributions#code-of-conduct).
      
      ## Security Vulnerabilities
      
      If you discover a security vulnerability within Laravel, please send an e-mail to Taylor Otwell via [taylor@laravel.com](mailto:taylor@laravel.com). All security vulnerabilities will be promptly addressed.
      
      ## License
      
      The Laravel framework is open-sourced software licensed under the [MIT license](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT).

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Models;

use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Factories\HasFactory;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Relations\BelongsTo;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\SoftDeletes;

class Assignment extends Model
{
    use HasFactory;
    use SoftDeletes;

    protected $fillable = [
        'project_id',
        'task_id',
        'resource_id',
        'role',
    ];

    protected $hidden = [
        'project_id',
        'task_id',
        'resource_id',
    ];

    public function project(): BelongsTo
    {
        return $this->belongsTo(Project::class);
    }

    public function task(): BelongsTo
    {
        return $this->belongsTo(Task::class);
    }

    public function resource(): BelongsTo
    {
        return $this->belongsTo(Resource::class);
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Models;

use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Concerns\HasUuids;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Factories\HasFactory;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Relations\BelongsTo;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Relations\HasMany;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\SoftDeletes;

class Task extends Model
{
    use HasFactory;
    use SoftDeletes;

    protected $fillable = [
        'project_id',
        'parent_id',
        'order',
        'name',
        'description',
        'start_input',
        'duration',
        'priority',
        'percent_complete',
        'task_type',
        'effective_start',
        'effective_end',
        'early_start',
        'early_finish',
        'late_start',
        'late_finish',
        'slack',
        'is_critical',
    ];

    protected $casts = [
        'order' => 'integer',
        'duration' => 'integer',
        'percent_complete' => 'integer',
        'slack' => 'integer',
        'is_critical' => 'boolean',
        'start_input' => 'date',
        'effective_start' => 'date',
        'effective_end' => 'date',
        'early_start' => 'date',
        'early_finish' => 'date',
        'late_start' => 'date',
        'late_finish' => 'date',
    ];

    protected $hidden = [
        'project_id',
        'parent_id',
    ];

    public function project(): BelongsTo
    {
        return $this->belongsTo(Project::class);
    }

    public function parent(): BelongsTo
    {
        return $this->belongsTo(Task::class, 'parent_id');
    }

    public function children(): HasMany
    {
        return $this->hasMany(Task::class, 'parent_id');
    }

    public function dependencies(): HasMany
    {
        return $this->hasMany(Dependency::class, 'predecessor_id');
    }

    public function dependents(): HasMany
    {
        return $this->hasMany(Dependency::class, 'successor_id');
    }

    public function assignments(): HasMany
    {
        return $this->hasMany(Assignment::class);
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Models;

// use Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\MustVerifyEmail;
use Database\Factories\UserFactory;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Attributes\Fillable;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Attributes\Hidden;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Factories\HasFactory;
use Illuminate\Foundation\Auth\User as Authenticatable;
use Illuminate\Notifications\Notifiable;

#[Fillable(['name', 'email', 'password'])]
#[Hidden(['password', 'remember_token'])]
class User extends Authenticatable
{
    /** @use HasFactory<UserFactory> */
    use HasFactory, Notifiable;

    /**
     * Get the attributes that should be cast.
     *
     * @return array<string, string>
     */
    protected function casts(): array
    {
        return [
            'email_verified_at' => 'datetime',
            'password' => 'hashed',
        ];
    }
}

> _Reasoning_
> There's already a scaffold: migrations, models (with salary encrypted + hidden — good), a seeder with sample data, a ProjectController + index view. Missing:
> 
> - docs/PRD.md (PRD is at root), docs/DECISIONS.md, docs/SUGGESTIONS.md
> - The scheduling engine in app/Domain/Scheduling (pure PHP) — nothing exists
> - Recalculation entry point + persistence of computed fields (the seeder never computes effective dates)
> - Livewire 3, Pest, Larastan not installed
> - UI: full app UI (projects CRUD, calendar, tasks, deps, resources, assignments, Gantt, PERT, CPM)
> - Localization en/id
> - composer scripts: check, test:mysql
> - TestsThe task from the user: "follow my prompt and casually do the PRD" — build P0 first, then P1.
> 
> Given the huge scope, let me define the plan and get to work. I will:
> 
> **Phase 0 — Setup/docs**
> 1. Move PRD → docs/PRD.md
> 2. docs/DECISIONS.md (start, keep appending)
> 3. docs/SUGGESTIONS.md
> 4. Install: livewire/livewire, pestphp/pest, larastan/larastan
> 5. composer.json scripts: check, test:mysql (phpunit.mysql.xml)
> 6. .env: DB_DATABASE=project_scheduler, dedicated DB user. Create DB + user in MariaDB via root CLI. Also update .env.example.
> 
> **Phase 1 — Engine (pure PHP)**
> app/Domain/Scheduling/:
> - `WorkingCalendar.php` — value object: working day numbers, holiday date ranges; isWorkingDay, nextWorkingDay, addWorkingDays, subtractWorkingDays, countWorkingDays.
> - `SchedulableTask.php` — DTO (id, parentId, order, name, requestedStart, duration)
> - `DependencyLink.php` — DTO (predecessorId, successorId, type, lag)
> - `ProjectScheduleInput.php` — calendar + tasks + links
> - `TaskSchedule.php` — result DTO: id, start, end, earlyStart/Finish, lateStart/Finish, slack, isCritical
> - `ScheduleResult.php` — collection + projectStart/projectEnd/totalDuration
> - `ScheduleEngine.php` — single entry: `calculate(ProjectScheduleInput): ScheduleResult`
> - `CycleDetector.php` — `findCycle(tasks, links): ?array<int>` returning task-id path
> - `DependencyGraph.php` maybe internal.
> 
> Where does enum for dependency type live? Pure PHP enum `DependencyType: string { Case FS, SS }` in Domain\Scheduling. 
> 
> **Phase 2 — App layer wiring**
> - `App\Support\Schedule\ScheduleRecalculator` (bridge, uses Eloquent to build input, calls engine, writes back). Hmm — where to put? Rule: engine lives in app/Domain/Scheduling pure. The bridge can be app/Services/Schedule/ProjectScheduleService.php. It has one method `recalculate(Project $project)` called from models' boot events? Simplest robust: call from Eloquent model events (saved/deleted on Task, Dependency, Holiday, Calendar) — CAL-5 "Any calendar change triggers recalculation", CPM-6 "updates automatically whenever data changes". Model observers in AppServiceProvider or an Observer class. But careful: during seeding bulk creation, recalc per save is slow but fine for demo; better use a `ScheduleRecalculator` invoked explicitly by Livewire components + observer for safety. I'll implement an Observer registered in AppServiceProvider for Task, Dependency, Holiday, Calendar (saved/deleted) that recalculates the affected project. Edge: during recalc we write task fields — avoid infinite loop by using `Task::withoutEvents` or updateQuietly. Use `saveQuietly`/`updateQuietly`.
> 
> Also cycle prevention service: `App\Services\Schedule\DependencyService` with `assertNoCycle(projectId, newEdge)` used by Livewire validation, returning cycle path names for message (DEP-5).
> 
> **Phase 3 — UI (Livewire 3)**
> Layout: resources/views/components/layouts/app.blade.php with Tailwind + Vite + language switcher.
> Livewire components (app/Livewire/...):
> - Projects: `Projects/Index` (list + create modal), `Projects/Show` (dashboard w/ tabs), `Projects/Edit`? Keep simple: single Show page with sections.
> Actually simpler: 
> - `ProjectIndex` — list, create (PRJ-1/2), delete with confirm.
> - `ProjectForm` — create/edit (name required).
> - `CalendarEditor` — working days checkboxes, weekend days auto-derived? PRD: CAL-1 define working days + hours; CAL-2 weekend days excluded. Simplest: working_days [1-5 default], weekend = the complement (auto). But migration has both fields. Decision: store working_days; weekend_days = 1..7 minus working_days (derived but stored for display). Editing: checkboxes for working days; weekend computed on save. Hours per day input. (CAL-1)
> - `HolidayManager` — add/edit/delete holidays with date/range (CAL-3).
> - `TaskIndex` — table with hierarchy indent, add/edit/delete/reorder(up/down), duration, priority, start date, parent select; show computed start/end, slack, critical badge, assigned members (ASN-2); predecessors editing with type+lag + cycle error (DEP-1..6); assignments checkbox list (ASN-1). Milestone duration=0 supported (TSK-5 P1). percent_complete input + progress bar (TSK-6 P1).
> - `ResourceIndex` — CRUD members incl. salary (encrypted), delete warning if assignments exist (RES-2), leave management per member (RES-3).
> - `GanttChart` — SVG: rows per task (indent), bars, weekend/holiday shading, dependency arrows, zoom day/week/month, today line, critical highlighting (red + thickness + icon), member names on bars, member filter (P1), leave warning badges (ASN-3 P1).
> - `PertChart` — SVG nodes with ES/EF/LS/LF/slack, arrows, click node → detail panel, pan/zoom (scroll + scale buttons).
> - Slack shown in task list (CPM-3), project end + duration header (CPM-4).
> 
> Localization: resources/lang/en/... and id/... — in Laravel 11+, lang files at resources/lang. Create `resources/lang/en/app.php`, `id/app.php` with all UI strings. Blade uses `__('app.key')`. Language switcher sets session locale. Default en.
> 
> Routes: routes/web.php with resource routes (Livewire full-page components or controller + views?). Use Livewire full-page components with #[Layout]. Hmm — Livewire 3 full-page components need `#[Layout('components.layouts.app')]`. Fine.
> 
> Route structure:
> ```
> / → ProjectIndex
> /projects/create → ProjectForm
> /projects/{project}/edit → ProjectForm/projects/{project} → ProjectDashboard (with tabs: tasks, calendar, resources, gantt, pert) — one Show page hosting child components? Simpler: separate pages:
> /projects/{project}/tasks/projects/{project}/calendar
> /projects/{project}/resources
> /projects/{project}/gantt
> /projects/{project}/pert
> ```
> 
> **Phase 4 — Tests (Pest)**
> - tests/Unit/Scheduling/: WorkingCalendarTest, ScheduleEngineTest (≥5 reference networks: FS chain, SS + lag, holidays, multiple predecessors max constraint, parent rollup, negative lag), CycleDetectorTest.
> - tests/Feature/: ProjectCrudTest (PRJ-1/2, default calendar auto-created), TaskTest (TSK-1 validation: positive duration, start moved to next working day; TSK-2 reorder; TSK-4 parent computed), DependencyTest (cycle prevention DEP-5, lag calc DEP-2/4), CalendarTest (CAL-5 holiday recalc shifts successors), ResourceTest (salary encrypted, hidden from JSON, RES-4), AssignmentTest (ASN-1/2).
> - Pest setup: tests/Pest.php with TestCase, RefreshDatabase.
> 
> **Phase 5 — verification**
> - npm install + build (for Vite assets); run migrations on MySQL, seed, `composer check`, `composer test:mysql`, paste output.
> - Commit with requirement IDs.
> 
> Pint: default preset laravel. Larastan: add phpstan.neon with level max? Use level 6ish. Larastan config: `parameters: level: 6, paths: [app]`, plus `checkMissingIterableValueType: false`? Newer Larastan handles it. Keep simple: level: 5 or 6 to be achievable.
> 
> composer.json scripts:
> ```json
> "check": [
>   "@test",
>   "@php vendor/bin/pint --test",
>   "@analyse"
> ],
> "test": [...existing],
> "test:mysql": "@php artisan test --configuration=phpunit.mysql.xml",
> "analyse": "@php vendor/bin/phpstan analyse --memory-limit=512M"
> ```
> phpunit.mysql.xml: copy of phpunit.xml with DB_CONNECTION=mysql, DB_DATABASE=project_scheduler (credentials from .env).

>     public function shift(DateTimeInterface $date, int $days): DateTimeImmutable // move n working days (negative ok); n=0 → adjust(date)?

> shift with n=0: return date unchanged (no adjustment) — but countWorkingDays for slack needs care. Let me define precisely:
> 
> - shift($date, $n): if $n > 0: move forward, counting only working days, $n steps. If $n < 0: move backward $n steps. $n == 0: return $date as-is.
> - countWorkingDays($from, $to): if $to < $from → -countWorkingDays($to,$from). Else count working days d with $from < d <= $to. So countWorkingDays(Mon, Mon)=0; countWorkingDays(Mon, Tue)=1 if Tue working.
> 
> Slack: LS and ES both working days (starts always on working days; milestone too). slack = countWorkingDays(ES, LS). 
> 
> Forward: effectiveStart = max(adjust(requestedStart), constraints). Constraints: FS: shift(predEnd, lag+1) — but predEnd is a working day; shift moves lag+1 working days forward → lands on working day. SS: shift(predStart, lag). Both land on working days. If no requested start → use default start (input field). If constraint > that, max wins. All results are working days. Edge: defaultStart also adjusted via adjust().
> 
> Milestone: duration 0 → end = start (start is working day).
> 
> Backward: for tasks w/o successors: LF = projectEnd (a working day). FS successor: latest finish for pred = shiftBack(succLS, lag+1) = shift(succLS, -(lag+1)); predLF = min over constraints. SS: latest start for pred = shift(succLS, -lag); since SS constrains predStart <= ..., predLF = that + duration-1 → shift(succLS, -lag + duration - 1)? Careful: predLS = shift(succLS, -lag); predLF = shift(predLS, duration-1). For milestone duration 0 → LF = LS.
> 
> Negative lag: FS with lag=-1: successor start = shift(predEnd, 0) = predEnd (same day). Backward: predLF = shift(succLS, -(-1+1)) = shift(succLS, 0) = succLS. Consistent.
> 
> Shift bounds: if shifting backward before calendar start of data, no working day found → cap at some minimum (e.g., loop forever?). > Internal algorithm in engine:
> - index tasks by id; children map; leaves = ids without children... but wait: leaf = no children. What about tasks whose parent exists — they're the schedulable set. Parent tasks (have children) derived.
> - Expand links: for each link, endpoints → leaf sets: leafDescendants(endpoint) = if endpoint is leaf → [endpoint]; if parent → all descendant leaves (recursively). If a parent has no leaf descendants (empty subtree or parent-with-no-children): then treat the parent itself as a schedulable node? Simplest: classify "parent" strictly as task having ≥1 child; a task with task_type='Parent' but no children acts as a normal leaf task. So leafDescendants returns descendants if any else [self].
> - Prevent ancestor cycles: skip links where successor ∈ leafDescendants include predecessor itself (self-loop after expansion, e.g., child→parent link expands to self edge) — validation at app layer forbids those; engine ignores self-edges.
> - topo sort leaves (Kahn). Cycle → throw.
> - forward: for each leaf in topo order: candidates = [defaultStart adjusted]; for each incoming expanded edge compute constraint; ES = max; EF = shift(ES, dur-1) (dur0 → ES).
> - parents bottom-up: sort parents by depth descending (deepest first). ES = min child ES; EF = max child EF; duration derived.
> - projectStart = min all ES (incl parents); projectFinish = max all EF.
> - backward: leaves in reverse topo: LF = min over outgoing expanded edges: FS: shift(succLS, -(lag+1)); SS: shift(succLS, -lag)... wait for SS, constrains pred's LS; then pred LF = LS + dur -1. So compute per-task LS/LF: first compute LS candidates: LF from successors; tasks with no successors LF = projectFinish. LS = shiftBack(LF, dur-1) = shift(LF, -(dur-1)); dur 0 → LS = LF. For FS edge: predLF_cand = shift(succLS, -(lag+1)). For SS: predLS_cand = shift(succLS, -lag) → then convert to LF: shift(that, dur-1). So track per task: lfFromFS (dates) and lsFromSS (dates); LS = min(shiftBack(minLf, dur-1), min lsFromSS); LF = shift(LS, dur-1).
> - slack = countWorkingDays(ES, LS); isCritical = slack === 0.
> - parents backward: LF = min child LF; LS = shiftBack(LF, parentDur-1)? Parent slack: standard: slack = countWorkingDays(ES, LS) where LF=min child LF, LS = shift(LF, -(span-1)) with span = countWorkingDays(ES,EF)+1. Critical if slack==0. Also ES=min child ES, EF = max child EF.
>

> final class WorkingCalendar
> {
>     /** @var array<int, true> */
>     private array $workingDayIndex;
>     /** @var array<string, true> */
>     private array $holidayIndex;
> 
>     /**
>      * @param  list<int>  $workingDays  ISO weekdays 1 (Mon) – 7 (Sun)
>      * @param  list<string>  $holidays  dates in Y-m-d
>      */
>     public function __construct(array $workingDays, array $holidays = [])
>     {
>         $workingDays = array_values(array_unique(array_map('intval', $workingDays)));
>         sort($workingDays);
>         if ($workingDays === [] || array_filter($workingDays, fn ($d) => $d < 1 || $d > 7) !== []) {
>             throw new SchedulingException('Working calendar needs at least one working day between 1 and 7.');
>         }
>         $this->workingDayIndex = array_fill_keys($workingDays, true);
>         $this->holidayIndex = array_fill_keys(array_map('strval', $holidays), true);
>     }
> 
>     public function isWorkingDay(DateTimeInterface $date): bool
>     {
>         $dt = DateTimeImmutable::createFromInterface($date);
>         $day = (int) $dt->format('w'); // 0=Sun..6=Sat
>         $iso = $day === 0 ? 7 : $day;
>         if (! isset($this->workingDayIndex[$iso])) return false;
>         return ! isset($this->holidayIndex[$dt->format('Y-m-d')]);
>     }
> 
>     /** Next working day strictly after $date. */
>     public function nextWorkingDay(DateTimeInterface $date): DateTimeImmutable
>     {
>         $dt = self::toImmutable($date)->setTime(0,0);
>         for ($i = 0; $i < 3660; $i++) {
>             $dt = $dt->modify('+1 day');
>             if ($this->isWorkingDay($dt)) return $dt;
>         }
>         throw new SchedulingException('No working day found within 10 years — check calendar configuration.');
>     }
> 
>     /** $date if it is a working day, otherwise the next working day. */
>     public function adjust(DateTimeInterface $date): DateTimeImmutable
>     {
>         $dt = self::toImmutable($date)->setTime(0, 0);
>         return $this->isWorkingDay($dt) ? $dt : $this->nextWorkingDay($dt);
>     }

>     /** Move ±$days working days (0 = same day, no adjustment). */

  "path": "app/Domain/Scheduling/WorkingCalendar.php",
  "instructions": "Working-day calendar value object with working-day arithmetic (no Eloquent)",
  "content": "<?php\n\ndeclare(strict_types=1);\n\nnamespace App\\Domain\\Scheduling;\n\nuse DateTimeImmutable;\nuse DateTimeInterface;\n\n/**\n * Working calendar: knows which days are working days (PRD CAL-1/CAL-2/CAL-3).\n *\n * Pure value object — no Eloquent, no facades. All working-day arithmetic\n * (PRD §8.1) happens through this class.\n */\nfinal class WorkingCalendar\n{\n    /** @var array<int, true> Set of ISO weekday numbers (1=Mon .. 7=Sun) that are working days */\n    private array $workingDays;\n\n    /** @var array<string, true> Set of holiday dates formatted Y-m-d */\n    private array $holidays;\n\n    /**\n     * @param  array<int, int>  $workingDays  ISO weekday numbers (1=Mon .. 7=Sun)\n     * @param  array<int, string>  $holidays  Holiday dates formatted Y-m-d\n     */\n    public function __construct(array $workingDays, array $holidays = [])\n    {\n        $workingDays = array_values(array_unique(array_map('intval', $workingDays)));\n        sort($workingDays);\n\n        if ($workingDays === [] || array_filter($workingDays, static fn (int $d): bool => $d < 1 || $d > 7) !== []) {\n            throw new SchedulingException('Working calendar requires at least one working day between 1 (Mon) and 7 (Sun).');\n        }\n\n        $this->workingDays = array_fill_keys($workingDays, true);\n        $this->holidays = array_fill_keys(array_map('strval', $holidays), true);\n    }\n\n    public function isWorkingDay(DateTimeInterface $date): bool\n    {\n        $day = (int) $date->format('w'); // 0=Sun .. 6=Sat\n        $iso = $day === 0 ? 7 : $day;\n\n        if (! isset($this->workingDays[$iso])) {\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        return ! isset($this->holidays[$date->format('Y-m-d')]);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * The given date if it is a working day, otherwise the next working day (TSK-1 AC).\n     */\n    public function adjust(DateTimeInterface $date): DateTimeImmutable\n    {\n        $current = self::immutable($date);\n\n        if ($this->isWorkingDay($current)) {\n            return $current;\n        }\n\n        return $this->nextWorkingDay($current);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * The next working day strictly after the given date.\n     */\n    public function nextWorkingDay(DateTimeInterface $date): DateTimeImmutable\n    {\n        $current = self::immutable($date);\n\n        for ($i = 0; $i < 3660; $i++) {\n            $current = $current->modify('+1 day');\n\n            if ($this->isWorkingDay($current)) {\n                return $current;\n            }\n        }\n\n        throw new SchedulingException('No working day found within ten years — check the calendar configuration.');\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Move forwards (positive) or backwards (negative) by whole working days.\n     * Shifting by zero returns the same calendar day.\n     */\n    public function shift(DateTimeInterface $date, int $workingDays): DateTimeImmutable\n    {\n        $current = self::immutable($date);\n        $step = $workingDays >= 0 ? 1 : -1;\n        $remaining = abs($workingDays);\n\n        for ($i = 0; $i < 366_000 && $remaining > 0; $i++) {\n            $current = $current->modify(sprintf('%+d day', $step));\n\n            if ($this->isWorkingDay($current)) {\n                $remaining--;\n            }\n        }\n\n        if ($remaining > 0) {\n            throw new SchedulingException('Could not shift by the requested number of working days — check the calendar configuration.');\n        }\n\n        return $current;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Number of working days strictly after $from, up to and including $to.\n     * Negative when $to is before $from.\n     */\n    public function countWorkingDays(DateTimeInterface $from, DateTimeInterface $to): int\n    {\n        $start = self::immutable($from);\n        $end = self::immutable($to);\n\n        if ($start == $end) {\n            return 0;\n        }\n\n        if ($start > $end) {\n            return -$this->countWorkingDays($end, $start);\n        }\n\n        $count = 0;\n        $cursor = $start;\n\n        while ($cursor < $end) {\n            $cursor = $cursor->modify('+1 day');\n\n            if ($this->isWorkingDay($cursor)) {\n                $count++;\n            }\n        }\n\n        return $count;\n    }\n\n    private static function immutable(DateTimeInterface $date): DateTimeImmutable\n    {\n        return DateTimeImmutable::createFromInterface($date)->setTime(0, 0);\n    }\n}\n"
}

Throws CircularDependencyException when a cycle exists.\n     *\n     * @return list<int>\n     */\n    public function topologicalOrder(): array\n    {\n        $inDegree = array_fill_keys($this->taskIds, 0);\n        $adjacency = array_fill_keys($this->taskIds, []);\n\n        foreach ($this->links as $link) {\n            if (! isset($inDegree[$link->predecessorId]) || ! isset($inDegree[$link->successorId])) {\n                continue; // edges outside the given task set are ignored\n            }\n\n            $adjacency[$link->predecessorId][] = $link->successorId;\n            $inDegree[$link->successorId]++;\n        }\n\n        $queue = [];\n        foreach ($inDegree as $id => $degree) {\n            if ($degree === 0) {\n                $queue[] = $id;\n            }\n        }\n\n        $order = [];\n        while ($queue !== []) {\n            $id = array_shift($queue);\n            $order[] = $id;\n\n            foreach ($adjacency[$id] as $next) {\n                $inDegree[$next]--;\n\n                if ($inDegree[$next] === 0) {\n                    $queue[] = $next;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        if (count($order) !== count($this->taskIds)) {\n            $remaining = array_values(array_diff($this->taskIds, $order));\n            throw new CircularDependencyException($this->findCycle($remaining));\n        }\n\n        return $order;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Depth-first search for one concrete cycle among the given nodes.\n     *\n     * @param  list<int>  $candidates\n     * @return list<int>\n     */\n    public function findCycle(array $candidates): array\n    {\n        $successors = array_fill_keys($candidates, []);\n        foreach ($this->links as $link) {\n            if (isset($successors[$link->predecessorId]) && isset($successors[$link->successorId])) {\n                $successors[$link->predecessorId][] = $link->successorId;\n            }\n        }\n\n        $state = []; // id => 1 visiting, 2 done\n        $stack = [];\n\n        $visit = function (int $id) use (&$visit, &$state, &$stack, $successors): array {\n            $state[$id] = 1;\n            $stack[] = $id;\n\n            foreach ($successors[$id] ?? [] as $next) {\n                if (($state[$next] ?? 0) === 1) {\n                    $at = array_search($next, $stack, true);\n\n                    return array_slice($stack, $at === false ? 0 : $at);\n                }\n\n                if (($state[$next] ?? 0) === 0) {\n                    $cycle = $visit($next);\n\n                    if ($cycle !== []) {\n                        return $cycle;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            array_pop($stack);\n            $state[$id] = 2;\n\n            return [];\n        };\n\n        foreach ($candidates as $id) {\n            if (($state[$id] ?? 0) === 0) {\n                $cycle = $visit($id);\n\n                if ($cycle !== []) {\n                    return $cycle;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        return $candidates;\n    }\n}\n"

  "instructions": "Bridge from Eloquent models to the pure engine and back",
  "content": "<?php\n\ndeclare(strict_types=1);\n\nnamespace App\\Services\\Schedule;\n\nuse App\\Domain\\Scheduling\\DependencyLink;\nuse App\\Domain\\Scheduling\\DependencyType;\nuse App\\Domain\\Scheduling\\SchedulableTask;\nuse App\\Domain\\Scheduling\\ProjectScheduleInput;\nuse App\\Domain\\Scheduling\\ScheduleEngine;\nuse App\\Domain\\Scheduling\\WorkingCalendar;\nuse App\\Models\\Calendar;\nuse App\\Models\\Holiday;\nuse App\\Models\\Project;\nuse App\\Models\\Task;\nuse DateTimeImmutable;\nuse Illuminate\\Support\\Facades\\DB;\n\n/**\n * The application-side bridge to the scheduling engine.\n *\n * Loads a project with Eloquent, converts it into pure domain DTOs, calls the\n * ONE recalculation entry point (ScheduleEngine::calculate) and persists the\n * calculated dates/slack/critical flags back onto the tasks (CPM-6).\n *\n * Views and controllers never compute dates — they only read what is written here.\n */\nfinal class ScheduleRecalculator\n{\n    public function __construct(private readonly ScheduleEngine $engine) {}\n\n    /**\n     * Recalculate and persist the whole schedule of a project (PRD §8.6).\n     */\n    public function recalculate(Project $project): void\n    {\n        $calendar = $project->calendar()->first();\n\n        if ($calendar === null) {\n            return; // no calendar yet — nothing sane to compute\n        }\n\n        $tasks = Task::query()\n            ->where('project_id', $project->id)\n            ->orderBy('order')\n            ->get();\n\n        $holidays = Holiday::query()\n            ->where('calendar_id', $calendar->id)\n            ->get();\n\n        $defaultStart = $tasks\n            ->pluck('start_input')\n            ->filter()\n            ->sort()\n            ->first() ?? now()->startOfDay();\n\n        $input = new ProjectScheduleInput(\n            calendar: $this->buildCalendar($calendar, $holidays),\n            tasks: $this->buildTasks($tasks),\n            links: $this->buildLinks($project),\n            defaultStart: DateTimeImmutable::createFromInterface($defaultStart->toDateTimeImmutable()),\n        );\n\n        $result = $this->engine->calculate($input);\n\n        DB::transaction(static function () use ($tasks, $result, $project, $calendar, $holidays): void {\n            foreach ($tasks as $task) {\n                $schedule = $result->forTask($task->id);\n\n                if ($schedule === null) {\n                    continue;\n                }\n\n                $task->forceFill([\n                    'effective_start' => $schedule->earlyStart->format('Y-m-d'),\n                    'effective_end' => $schedule->earlyFinish->format('Y-m-d'),\n                    'early_start' => $schedule->earlyStart->format('Y-m-d'),\n                    'early_finish' => $schedule->earlyFinish->format('Y-m-d'),\n                    'late_start' => $schedule->lateStart->format('Y-m-d'),\n                    'late_finish' => $schedule->lateFinish->format('Y-m-d'),\n                    'slack' => $schedule->slack,\n                    'is_critical' => $schedule->isCritical,\n                ])->saveQuietly();\n            }\n\n            // Keep the legacy JSON mirror in sync; the holidays table is the source of truth (D-15).\n            $calendar->forceFill([\n                'holidays' => $holidays->map(static fn (Holiday $holiday): array => [\n                    'id' => (string) $holiday->id,\n                    'name' => $holiday->name,\n                    'date' => $holiday->date->format('Y-m-d'),\n                    'end_date' => $holiday->end_date?->format('Y-m-d'),\n                ])->values()->all(),\n            ])->saveQuietly();\n\n            $project->forceFill([\n                'started_at' => $result->projectStart->format('Y-m-d'),\n                'completed_at' => $result->projectFinish->format('Y-m-d'),\n            ])->saveQuietly();\n        });\n    }\n\n    private function buildCalendar(Calendar $calendar, $holidays): WorkingCalendar\n    {\n        $dates = [];\n\n        foreach ($holidays as $holiday) {\n            $start = $holiday->date->toImmutable()->startOfDay();\n            $end = $holiday->end_date?->toImmutable()->startOfDay() ?? $start;\n\n            for ($date = $start; $date <= $end; $date = $date->addDay()) {\n                $dates[] = $date->format('Y-m-d');\n            }\n        }\n\n        return new WorkingCalendar($calendar->working_days ?? [], array_values(array_unique($dates)));\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @param  \\Illuminate\\Database\\Eloquent\\Collection<int, Task>  $tasks\n     * @return list<SchedulableTask>\n     */\n    private function buildTasks($tasks): array\n    {\n        return $tasks->map(static fn (Task $task): SchedulableTask => new SchedulableTask(\n            id: $task->id,\n            parentId: $task->parent_id,\n            position: $task->order,\n            name: $task->name,\n            requestedStart: $task->start_input === null\n                ? null\n                : DateTimeImmutable::createFromInterface($task->start_input->toDateTimeImmutable()),\n            duration: $task->duration,\n        ))->all();\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @return list<DependencyLink>\n     */\n    private function buildLinks(Project $project): array\n    {\n        return $project->dependencies()\n            ->get()\n            ->map(static fn ($dependency): DependencyLink => new DependencyLink(\n                predecessorId: $dependency->predecessor_id,\n                successorId: $dependency->successor_id,\n                type: DependencyType::from($dependency->type),\n                lag: $dependency->lag,\n            ))->all();\n    }\n}\n"
}

{
  "path": "app/Services/Schedule/DependencyValidator.php",
  "instructions": "Save-time cycle prevention and hierarchy integrity checks",
  "content": "<?php\n\ndeclare(strict_types=1);\n\nnamespace App\\Services\\Schedule;\n\nuse App\\Domain\\Scheduling\\CircularDependencyException;\nuse App\\Domain\\Scheduling\\DependencyGraph;\nuse App\\Domain\\Scheduling\\DependencyLink;\nuse App\\Models\\Dependency;\nuse App\\Models\\Project;\nuse App\\Models\\Task;\n\n/**\n * Application-level integrity rules for dependencies and task hierarchy\n * (PRD DEP-5, §8.7: data must never be saved in a state with a dependency cycle).\n *\n * Mirrors what the engine enforces, so bad data is rejected *before* it is written.\n */\nfinal class DependencyValidator\n{\n    /**\n     * Validate a candidate dependency (predecessor -> successor).\n     *\n     * @return list<string> human-readable errors; empty means valid\n     */\n    public function validateDependency(Project $project, Task $predecessor, Task $successor, string $type, int $lag): array\n    {\n        $errors = [];\n\n        if ($predecessor->project_id !== $project->id || $successor->project_id !== $project->id) {\n            $errors[] = 'Both tasks must belong to this project.';\n        }\n\n        if (! in_array($type, ['FS', 'SS'], true)) {\n            $errors[] = 'Dependency type must be FS or SS.';\n        }\n\n        if ($predecessor->id === $successor->id) {\n            $errors[] = 'A task cannot depend on itself.';\n        }\n\n        if ($this->isAncestorOf($predecessor->id, $successor->id, $project)) {\n            $errors[] = 'A task cannot depend on one of its own sub-activities.';\n        }\n\n        if ($this->isAncestorOf($successor->id, $predecessor->id, $project)) {\n            $errors[] = 'A sub-activity cannot be a predecessor of its own parent.';\n        }\n\n        if ($errors === []) {\n            $cycle = $this->findCycle($project, $predecessor->id, $successor->id);\n\n            if ($cycle !== null) {\n                $errors[] = $this->cycleMessage($project, $cycle);\n            }\n        }\n\n        return $errors;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Would adding this edge create a cycle? Returns the id path (A -> B -> C -> A) or null.\n     *\n     * @param  list<array{predecessor_id: int, successor_id: int}>  $extra\n     * @return list<int>|null\n     */\n    public function findCycle(Project $project, int $predecessorId, int $successorId): ?array\n    {\n        $tasks = Task::query()->where('project_id', $project->id)->get();\n\n        $links = Dependency::query()\n            ->where('project_id', $project->id)\n            ->get()\n            ->map(static fn (Dependency $dependency): DependencyLink => new DependencyLink(\n                predecessorId: $dependency->predecessor_id,\n                successorId: $dependency->successor_id,\n                type: \\App\\Domain\\Scheduling\\DependencyType::from($dependency->type),\n                lag: $dependency->lag,\n            ))\n            ->all();\n\n        $links[] = new DependencyLink($predecessorId, $successorId, \\App\\Domain\\Scheduling\\DependencyType::FS, 0);\n\n        try {\n            (new DependencyGraph($tasks->pluck('id')->all(), $links))->topologicalOrder();\n        } catch (CircularDependencyException $exception) {\n            return $exception->cyclePath;\n        }\n\n        return null;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Map an id path to a display message naming the tasks (DEP-5).\n     *\n     * @param  list<int>  $cycle\n     */\n    public function cycleMessage(Project $project, array $cycle): string\n    {\n        $names = Task::query()\n            ->where('project_id', $project->id)\n            ->whereIn('id', $cycle)\n            ->pluck('name', 'id');\n\n        $labels = array_map(\n            static fn (int $id): string => (string) ($names[$id] ?? \"#{$id}\"),\n            $cycle,\n        );\n\n        $labels[] = $labels[0];\n\n        return 'Circular dependency detected: '.implode(' -> ', $labels);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Is $ancestorId an ancestor of $taskId (or the same task)?\n     */\n    public function isAncestorOf(int $ancestorId, int $taskId, Project $project): bool\n    {\n        $parents = Task::query()\n            ->where('project_id', $project->id)\n            ->pluck('parent_id', 'id');\n\n        $current = $taskId;\n\n        while (isset($parents[$current])) {\n            if ($parents[$current] === null) {\n                break;\n            }\n\n            if ($parents[$current] === $ancestorId) {\n                return true;\n            }\n\n            $current = $parents[$current];\n        }\n\n        return $ancestorId === $taskId && false; // self handled separately\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Depth of a task in the hierarchy (0 = top level); guard for the 4-level [A] limit.\n     */\n    public function depthOf(int $taskId, Project $project): int\n    {\n        $parents = Task::query()\n            ->where('project_id', $project->id)\n            ->pluck('parent_id', 'id');\n\n        $depth = 0;\n        $current = $taskId;\n\n        while (isset($parents[$current]) && $parents[$current] !== null) {\n            $depth++;\n            $current = (int) $parents[$current];\n        }\n\n        return $depth;\n    }\n}\n"
}

  "content": "<?php\n\ndeclare(strict_types=1);\n\nnamespace App\\Observers;\n\nuse App\\Models\\Calendar;\nuse App\\Models\\Dependency;\nuse App\\Models\\Holiday;\nuse App\\Models\\Project;\nuse App\\Models\\Task;\nuse App\\Services\\Schedule\\ScheduleRecalculator;\nuse Illuminate\\Database\\Eloquent\\Model;\n\n/**\n * Any change to scheduling data recalculates the whole project schedule\n * (PRD CAL-5, CPM-6, §8.6).\n *\n * Recalculated fields are written with saveQuietly(), so no recursion occurs.\n */\nfinal class ScheduleObserver\n{\n    public function __construct(private readonly ScheduleRecalculator $recalculator) {}\n\n    public function saved(Model $model): void\n    {\n        $this->recalculateFor($model);\n    }\n\n    public function deleted(Model $model): void\n    {\n        $this->recalculateFor($model);\n    }\n\n    private function recalculateFor(Model $model): void\n    {\n        $projectId = match (true) {\n            $model instanceof Task => $model->project_id,\n            $model instanceof Dependency => $model->project_id,\n            $model instanceof Calendar => $model->project_id,\n            $model instanceof Holiday => $model->calendar()->value('project_id'),\n            default => null,\n        };\n\n        if ($projectId === null) {\n            return;\n        }\n\n        $project = Project::query()->find($projectId);\n\n        if ($project === null) {\n            return;\n        }\n\n        $this->recalculator->recalculate($project);\n    }\n}\n"
}

    */\n    private static function moveableHolidays(int $year): array\n    {\n        return match ($year) {\n            2026 => [\n                ['name' => 'Nyepi (Tahun Baru Saka) / Balinese New $year): array\n    {\n        $holidays = array_merge(self::fixedDateHolidays($year), self::moveableHolidays($year));\n\n        usort($holidays, static fn (array $a, array $b): int => $holiday): bool\n    {\n        $date = DateTimeImmutable::createFromFormat('!Y-m-d', $holiday['date']);\n\n        return $date !== false && $date->format('Y-m-d') === $holiday['date'];\n    }\n}\n"

**🛠 Str Replace**

```json
{
  "path": "app/Domain/Scheduling/ScheduleEngine.php",
  "replacements": [
    {
      "oldString": "        [$lateStart, $lateFinish] = $this->backwardPass($input, $tasks, $leaves, $links, $projectFinish);\n        $this->rollUpParentsBackward($tasks, $children, $lateStart, $lateFinish);",
      "newString": "        [$lateStart, $lateFinish] = $this->backwardPass($input, $tasks, $leaves, $links, $projectFinish);\n        $this->rollUpParentsBackward($input, $tasks, $children, $earlyStart, $earlyFinish, $lateStart, $lateFinish);",
      "allowMultiple": false
    },
    {
      "oldString": "     * @param  array<int, list<int>>  $children\n     * @param  array<int, DateTimeImmutable>  $lateStart\n     * @param  array<int, DateTimeImmutable>  $lateFinish\n     */\n    private function rollUpParentsBackward(array $tasks, array $children, array &$lateStart, array &$lateFinish): void\n    {\n        foreach ($this->parentsByDepthDesc($tasks, $children) as $id) {\n            $childFinishes = [];\n            foreach ($children[$id] as $child) {\n                $childFinishes[] = $lateFinish[$child];\n            }\n\n            $lateFinish[$id] = $this->maxDate($childFinishes);\n        }\n    }",
      "newString": "     * @param  array<int, list<int>>  $children\n     * @param  array<int, DateTimeImmutable>  $earlyStart\n     * @param  array<int, DateTimeImmutable>  $earlyFinish\n     * @param  array<int, DateTimeImmutable>  $lateStart\n     * @param  array<int, DateTimeImmutable>  $lateFinish\n     */\n    private function rollUpParentsBackward(ProjectScheduleInput $input, array $tasks, array $children, array $earlyStart, array $earlyFinish, array &$lateStart, array &$lateFinish): void\n    {\n        $calendar = $input->calendar;\n\n        foreach ($this->parentsByDepthDesc($tasks, $children) as $id) {\n            $childFinishes = [];\n            foreach ($children[$id] as $child) {\n                $childFinishes[] = $lateFinish[$child];\n            }\n\n            $lateFinish[$id] = $this->maxDate($childFinishes);\n\n            // Late start derived from the parent's rolled-up span.\n            $span = $calendar->countWorkingDays($earlyStart[$id], $earlyFinish[$id]) + 1;\n            $lateStart[$id] = $calendar->shift($lateFinish[$id], -($span - 1));\n        }\n    }",
      "allowMultiple": false
    }
  ]
}

  "content": "<?php\n\ndeclare(strict_types=1);\n\nnamespace App\\Livewire\\Projects;\n\nuse App\\Models\\Project;\nuse Livewire\\Attributes\\Layout;\nuse Livewire\\Attributes\\Validate;\nuse Livewire\\Component;\n\n/**\n * PRJ-1 (create with name/organization/description) and PRJ-2 (list, open,\n * edit link, delete with confirmation).\n */\n#[Layout('components.layouts.app')]\nclass Index extends Component\n{\n    #[Validate('required|string|max:255')]\n    public string $name = '';\n\n    #[Validate('nullable|string|max:255')]\n    public string $organization = '';\n\n    #[Validate('nullable|string|max:2000')]\n    public string $description = '';\n\n    public bool $showCreate = false;\n\n    public ?int $deleteId = null;\n\n    public function create(): void\n    {\n        $this->validate();\n\n        $project = Project::create([\n            'name' => $this->name,\n            'organization' => $this->organization ?: null,\n            'description' => $this->description ?: null,\n        ]);\n\n        $this->reset(['name', 'organization', 'description', 'showCreate']);\n\n        $this->redirectRoute('projects.show', $project);\n    }\n\n    public function askDelete(int $projectId): void\n    {\n        $this->deleteId = $projectId;\n    }\n\n    public function cancelDelete(): void\n    {\n        $this->deleteId = null;\n    }\n\n    public function delete(): void\n    {\n        Project::findOrFail($this->deleteId)->delete();\n        $this->deleteId = null;\n    }\n\n    public function render()\n    {\n        return view('livewire.projects.index', [\n            'projects' => Project::query()->withCount(['tasks', 'resources'])->latest()->get(),\n        ]);\n    }\n}\n"
}

Empty name is rejected with a\n * clear message (PRJ-1 AC).\n */\n#[Layout('components.layouts.app')]\nclass Form extends Component\n{\n    public ?Project $project = null;\n\n    #[Validate('required|string|max:255')]\n    public string $name = '';\n\n    #[Validate('nullable|string|max:255')]\n    public string $organization = '';\n\n    #[Validate('nullable|string|max:2000')]\n    public string $description = '';\n\n    public function mount(?Project $project = null): void\n    {\n        $this->project = $project;\n\n        if ($project !== null) {\n            $this->name = $project->name;\n            $this->organization = (string) $project->organization;\n            $this->description = (string) $project->description;\n        }\n    }\n\n    public function save(): void\n    {\n        $this->validate();\n\n        $data = [\n            'name' => $this->name,\n            'organization' => $this->organization ?: null,\n            'description' => $this->description ?: null,\n        ];\n\n        if ($this->project === null) {\n            $project = Project::create($data);\n            $this->redirectRoute('projects.show', $project);\n\n            return;\n        }\n\n        $this->project->update($data);\n\n        $this->redirectRoute('projects.show', $this->project);\n    }\n\n    public function render()\n    {\n        return view('livewire.projects.form');\n    }\n}\n"
}

> _Reasoning_
> Careful: in Show, totalDuration as calendar diff days would include weekends — project duration should be working days. The recalc stores started_at/completed_at as project start/end dates. Total working days... I could recompute via WorkingCalendar quickly, or store. Better: compute working days with the pure calendar in the component? Rule says dates/slack computed only in engine — the total duration is a scheduling value; computing it in the view layer violates the spirit. Options: engine already returns totalDuration but we don't persist it. Add columns? Simpler: in Show, instantiate WorkingCalendar (domain class, allowed — it's the engine's calendar) and call countWorkingDays — that's using the domain, not reimplementing in Blade. It's still "computation outside the single entry point" though. Hmm.
> 
> Cleanest: persist total duration on projects table. But migrations already "shipped" — uncommitted, so I can edit the projects migration: add `unsignedInteger('total_duration')->nullable()` (working days). Recalc writes it. Show displays. Let me do that — cleaner and honors the single-entry-point rule.

Any change triggers recalculation via the observer\n * (CAL-5).\n */\n#[Layout('components.layouts.app')]\nclass Index extends Component\n{\n    public Project $project;\n\n    public Calendar $calendar;\n\n    /** @var list<int> */\n    #[Validate('required|array|min:1')]\n    #[Validate('each', values: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7])]\n    public array $workingDays = [];\n\n    #[Validate('required|integer|min:1|max:24')]\n    public int $hoursPerDay = 8;\n\n    // Holiday form\n    public ?int $holidayId = null;\n\n    #[Validate('required|string|max:255')]\n    public string $holidayName = '';\n\n    #[Validate('required|date')]\n    public string $holidayDate = '';\n\n    #[Validate('nullable|date|after_or_equal:holidayDate')]\n    public string $holidayEndDate = '';\n\n    // CAL-4 import\n    public int $importYear;\n\n    public function mount(Project $project): void\n    {\n        $this->project = $project;\n        $this->calendar = $project->calendar()->firstOrFail();\n        $this->workingDays = array_map('intval', $this->calendar->working_days ?? []);\n        $this->hoursPerDay = (int) $this->calendar->working_hours_per_day;\n        $this->importYear = now()->year;\n    }\n\n    public function saveCalendar(): void\n    {\n        $this->validate();\n\n        $workingDays = collect($this->workingDays)->unique()->sort()->values();\n\n        $this->calendar->update([\n            'working_days' => $workingDays->all(),\n            'weekend_days' => array_values(array_diff([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7], $workingDays->all())),\n            'working_hours_per_day' => $this->hoursPerDay,\n        ]);\n    }\n\n    public function saveHoliday(): void\n    {\n        $this->validate();\n\n        $data = [\n            'name' => $this->holidayName,\n            'date' => $this->holidayDate,\n            'end_date' => $this->holidayEndDate ?: null,\n        ];\n\n        if ($this->holidayId === null) {\n            $this->calendar->holidays()->create($data);\n        } else {\n            Holiday::query()\n                ->where('calendar_id', $this->calendar->id)\n                ->findOrFail($this->holidayId)\n                ->update($data);\n        }\n\n        $this->resetHolidayForm();\n    }\n\n    public function editHoliday(int $holidayId): void\n    {\n        $holiday = Holiday::query()\n            ->where('calendar_id', $this->calendar->id)\n            ->findOrFail($holidayId);\n\n        $this->holidayId = $holiday->id;\n        $this->holidayName = $holiday->name;\n        $this->holidayDate = $holiday->date->format('Y-m-d');\n        $this->holidayEndDate = $holiday->end_date?->format('Y-m-d') ?? '';\n    }\n\n    public function deleteHoliday(int $holidayId): void\n    {\n        Holiday::query()\n            ->where('calendar_id', $this->calendar->id)\n            ->findOrFail($holidayId)\n            ->delete();\n\n        if ($this->holidayId === $holidayId) {\n            $this->resetHolidayForm();\n        }\n    }\n\n    public function cancelHoliday(): void\n    {\n        $this->resetHolidayForm();\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * CAL-4: import the curated Indonesian national holiday template.\n     */\n    public function importTemplate(): void\n    {\n        $existing = $this->calendar->holidays()\n            ->get()\n            ->map(static fn (Holiday $holiday): string => $holiday->date->format('Y-m-d'))\n            ->all();\n\n        foreach (IndonesianHolidayTemplate::forYear($this->importYear) as $holiday) {\n            if (in_array($holiday['date'], $existing, true)) {\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            $this->calendar->holidays()->create([\n                'name' => $holiday['name'],\n                'date' => $holiday['date'],\n            ]);\n\n            $existing[] = $holiday['date'];\n        }\n    }\n\n    private function resetHolidayForm(): void\n    {\n        $this->reset(['holidayId', 'holidayName', 'holidayDate', 'holidayEndDate']);\n    }\n\n    public function render()\n    {\n        return view('livewire.calendar.index', [\n            'weekdays' => [\n                1 => __('calendar.mon'), 2 => __('calendar.tue'), 3 => __('calendar.wed'),\n                4 => __('calendar.thu'), 5 => __('calendar.fri'), 6 => __('calendar.sat'), 7 => __('calendar.sun'),\n            ],\n            'holidays' => $this->calendar->holidays()->orderBy('date')->get(),\n            'weekendDays' => array_values(array_diff([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7], $this->workingDays)),\n            'importYears' => IndonesianHolidayTemplate::availableYears(),\n        ]);\n    }\n}\n"
}

> _Reasoning_
> Now the Tasks component — the biggest. Let me design carefully.
> 
> Data:
> - project, tasks flat with depth (ordered tree), resources (for assignments), memberFilter.
> - Modal form for create/edit: name, description, start_input, duration (0 = milestone), priority, percent_complete, parent_id, assigned_resource_ids[], predecessors editor.
> - predecessor editor: array of rows [{id (existing dep id or null), task_id, type, lag}]. In mount/edit: load existing predecessors as rows. Add row button appends empty row. Save: validate each row (task_id required, not self, no cycle). Errors displayed per-row or general.
> 
> Simpler robust approach for deps: separate small section under task modal:
> - list current predecessors w/ remove buttons (wire:click removePredecessor(depId))
> - add form: select predecessor task, type, lag → addPredecessor()
> Adding validates cycle immediately (DEP-5) — show error message. Store as component property newPred = ['task_id'=>null,'type'=>'FS','lag'=>0].
> 
> This avoids complex array binding. Dependencies saved immediately on add/remove (not deferred to save), task fields saved via save(). 
> 
> Component state:
> ```php
> public Project $project;
> public bool $showModal = false;
> public ?int $editingId = null;
> public string $name = ''; public string $description = ''; public ?string $startInput = null;
> public int $duration = 1; public string $priority = 'Medium'; public int $percentComplete = 0;
> public ?int $parentId = null;
> public array $assignedResourceIds = [];
> public ?int $selectedTaskId = null; // for deps panelpublic array $newPred = ['task_id' => null, 'type' => 'FS', 'lag' => 0];
> public array $depErrors = [];
> public ?int $memberFilter = null;
> ```
> 
> Methods: create modal open (resetForm), edit(taskId) loads, save(), delete(id) w/ confirm flag, moveUp/moveDown among siblings, indent/outdent (TSK-7), addPredecessor, removePredecessor(depId).
> 
> save():
> - validate: name required max255; duration integer min0 max 3650; priority Rule::in(['Low','Medium','High','Critical']); percent 0-100; startInput nullable date; parentId nullable integer + custom: not self, not descendant, depth limit: if parent: depthOf(parent) + 1 <= 4.
> - create or update; sync assignments: Assignment::where('task_id')->pluck resource_ids sync($assignedResourceIds) — need project_id + role on assignments; role = resource->role.
> 
> Hierarchy helpers via DependencyValidator->depthOf + isAncestorOf.
> 
> Warnings (ASN-3, P1): in computed list: for each task (effective dates), for each assignment (resource), check: leave overlap (resource leaves overlapping effective range) or overlapping other tasks assigned to same resource. Compute warnings map resourceId => messages in render PHP. Keep it in the component render (PHP layer, reading persisted dates — acceptable; not "scheduling computation").
> 
> Tree flattening: fetch tasks ordered by (order)? Need depth-first ordering: build tree: order by order, then recursive: get top-level ordered by order; recurse children. Compute depth. I'll do in render: 
> 
> ```php
> $tasks = $this->project->tasks()->orderBy('order')->get();
> $byParent = $tasks->groupBy('parent_id');
> $rows = [];
> $walk = function ($parentId, $depth) use (&$walk, &$rows, $byParent) {
>     foreach ($byParent[$parentId] ?? [] as $task) {
>         $rows[] = ['task' => $task, 'depth' => $depth];
>         $walk($task->id, $depth + 1);
>     }
> };
> $walk(null, 0);
> ```
> 
> Filter by member: keep only tasks with assignment to member + their ancestors (to preserve hierarchy display)? Simpler: filter rows to those assigned to member; depth indentation kept. I'll filter rows to matching tasks (and show ancestors? simpler: just matching tasks). Decision: show matching tasks only.
> 
> Reorder among siblings: siblings = tasks with same parent_id ordered by order; moveUp: find index, swap orders with previous. Save via update (observer recalcs).
> 
> indent(task): siblings ordered; previous sibling becomes parent. outdent: parent's parent becomes parent (may be null). Guard depth ≤4. TSK-7 P1.
> 
> Milestone: task_type column exists; when duration == 0 → task_type 'Milestone'; if has children → 'Parent'; else 'Task'. Set on save + on parent changes. Display: diamond icon for milestone.
> 
> Modal predecessor panel: shows only when editing existing task (can't add deps to unsaved task). Deps for other tasks can reference it later anyway.
> 
> Priority select options.
> 
> Validation messages via lang keys: tasks.errors.* custom messages in rules() arrays.
> 
> Now write the component. It'll be long. Then the view.

Now the biggest piece — the Tasks manager (TSK-1..4 P0 + milestone/%complete/indent P1, DEP-1..6, assignments + warnings):

return $this->project->tasks()\n            ->where('parent_id', $task->parent_id)\n            ->orderBy('order')\n            ->get();\n    }\n\n    private function findTask(int $taskId): Task\n    {\n        return Task::query()\n            ->where('project_id', $this->project->id)\n            ->findOrFail($taskId);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Keep the denormalised task_type in sync: Milestone > Note: `Resource` model has SoftDeletes; `$resource->trashed()` fine. But resources() relation default excludes trashed. OK.
> 
> One issue: in `save()`, for a new task with parent, order = max order of that parent's children. Fine.
> 
> `moveUp/moveDown` swap orders — fine.
> 
> `indent` depth check uses depthOf(newParent)+1 >= 4 → depth of task becomes depthOf(newParent)+1; allowed up to 4 levels (depth 0..3). depthOf(parent)+1 >= 4 fails at making depth 4 (5th level). Correct: max depth index 3 = 4 levels.
> 
> Wait, but there's a subtlety in save() validation: depthOf($value)+1 >= 4 — same.
> 
> Also in save(): for edit where parent unchanged, fine.
