```
  content: |
      # PRD: Project Scheduling Application for Development Teams
      
      **Status:** Draft 0.1 | **Owner:** (TBD) | **Date:** October 9, 2026
      
      > This draft is based on an initial feature description. Anything not yet known is written as an **assumption** (marked [A]) or an **open question** (section 14) so it can be validated before development begins.
      
      ## 1. Summary
      
      An application for building, calculating, and visualizing software project schedules. Users create a project, structure tasks hierarchically with dependencies, set up working calendars and team member leave, and then view the result as a Gantt Chart, a PERT/Network Diagram, and a critical path. The system automatically calculates task dates from durations, dependencies, and calendars.
      
      ## 2. Background and Problem Statement
      
      Project managers and tech leads of development teams struggle to build and track realistic schedules because task dependencies, holidays, and team availability must be calculated manually (usually in spreadsheets). As a result, schedules are error-prone, hard to update when things change, and delay risk (the critical path) stays invisible.
      
      **Supporting evidence:** none yet. Needs to be gathered through interviews with 5-8 PMs/tech leads and samples of the schedules they use today (see section 14).
      
      ## 3. Goals and Non-Goals
      
      ### Goals
      
      1. Speed up creation of an initial project schedule compared with manual methods.
      2. Produce correct task dates automatically from dependencies and calendars.
      3. Make the critical path clearly visible so delay risks can be anticipated.
      4. Provide a visual overview of the schedule (Gantt and PERT) that is easy to share.
      
      ### Non-Goals (first version)
      
      - Project cost/budget calculation from salaries.
      - Automatic resource leveling.
      - Real-time multi-user collaboration.
      - Time tracking and timesheets.
      - Third-party integrations (Jira, Slack, etc.).
      
      ## 4. Users and Scenarios
      
      | Persona                                   | Description                                     | Key needs                                                                  |
      | ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
      | **Project Manager / Tech Lead** (primary) | Builds and maintains software project schedules | Build schedules quickly, see the impact of changes, find the critical path |
      | **Team member** [A]                       | Task recipient                                  | View their tasks and schedule (read-only in v1)                            |
      | **Stakeholder** [A]                       | Management/client                               | View a schedule summary via export                                         |
      
      **Primary scenario:** A PM creates a new project, sets the working calendar, enters tasks and sub-tasks, links them with dependencies, assigns team members, then opens the Gantt chart and critical path to check whether the deadline is achievable. When a task slips or a member goes on leave, the PM changes the data and sees the schedule recalculated.
      
      ## 5. Success Metrics
      
      | Metric                                                                                                      | Baseline               | Target (proposed)                 |
      | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- | --------------------------------- |
      | Time to build an initial schedule for a 50-task project                                                     | Measure current method | At least 50% reduction            |
      | Correctness of date and critical path calculations                                                          | -                      | 100% pass on reference test cases |
      | Users who build a complete schedule (project with tasks, dependencies, assignments) within the first 7 days | -                      | 40%                               |
      | Projects whose schedule is updated more than once                                                           | -                      | 50%                               |
      | User satisfaction (SUS or short survey)                                                                     | -                      | Score of 70 or higher             |
      
      Baselines and targets need to be validated with the product owner.
      
      ## 6. Scope
      
      **In scope (MVP):** all modules in section 7, with FS and SS dependencies, one calendar per project, per-member leave calendars, Gantt, PERT, and critical path.
      
      **Deferred:** cost from salaries, FF/SF, resource leveling, advanced baseline and progress tracking, notifications, real-time collaboration, MS Project import, mobile app.
      
      ## 7. Functional Requirements
      
      Priority: **P0** required for MVP, **P1** should have, **P2** later.
      
      ### 7.1 Project Management
      
      | ID    | Requirement                                                                                   | Priority |
      | ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
      | PRJ-1 | Users can create a project with a **name** (required), **organization**, and **description**. | P0       |
      | PRJ-2 | Users can view the project list, open, edit, and delete projects (with confirmation).         | P0       |
      | PRJ-3 | Users can duplicate a project as a template.                                                  | P2       |
      
      **Acceptance criteria for PRJ-1:** an empty name is rejected with a clear message; the project is saved and appears in the list; a default calendar is created automatically.
      
      ### 7.2 Working Calendar
      
      | ID    | Requirement                                                                                               | Priority |
      | ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
      | CAL-1 | Users define the **working days** per week and working hours per day [A: default Monday-Friday, 8 hours]. | P0       |
      | CAL-2 | Users define **weekend** days that are excluded from calculations.                                        | P0       |
      | CAL-3 | Users add, edit, and delete **custom/national holidays** (date, name, optional date range).               | P0       |
      | CAL-4 | Import the Indonesian national holiday list as a template.                                                | P1       |
      | CAL-5 | Any calendar change triggers recalculation of the whole schedule.                                         | P0       |
      
      **Acceptance criteria for CAL-5:** after adding a holiday in the middle of a task's range, the task's end date shifts accordingly and successor tasks shift with it.
      
      ### 7.3 Task Management
      
      | ID    | Requirement                                                                                                                               | Priority |
      | ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
      | TSK-1 | Users add tasks with a **name**, **start date**, **duration** (working days), and **priority** (Low/Medium/High/Critical).                | P0       |
      | TSK-2 | Users edit, delete, and reorder tasks.                                                                                                    | P0       |
      | TSK-3 | **Sub-activities:** tasks can be nested under a parent task (hierarchy up to [A] 4 levels).                                               | P0       |
      | TSK-4 | Parent tasks are calculated automatically from their children (earliest start to latest finish); parent duration is not entered manually. | P0       |
      | TSK-5 | **Milestone** task type (duration 0).                                                                                                     | P1       |
      | TSK-6 | Additional fields: description, percent complete.                                                                                         | P1       |
      | TSK-7 | Indent/outdent to change task level, and copy/paste tasks.                                                                                | P1       |
      
      **Acceptance criteria for TSK-1:** duration must be a positive number; a start date falling on a non-working day is automatically moved to the next working day; the end date is calculated from duration and calendar.
      
      ### 7.4 Task Dependencies
      
      | ID    | Requirement                                                                               | Priority |
      | ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
      | DEP-1 | Users set one or more **predecessors** on a task.                                         | P0       |
      | DEP-2 | **Finish-to-Start (FS)**: the task starts after its predecessor finishes.                 | P0       |
      | DEP-3 | **Start-to-Start (SS)**: the task starts together with or after its predecessor starts.   | P0       |
      | DEP-4 | **Delay/lag** in working days between tasks (negative lag/lead allowed [A]).              | P0       |
      | DEP-5 | The system **prevents circular dependencies** and shows a message identifying the cycle.  | P0       |
      | DEP-6 | When a task has several predecessors, its start date is taken from the latest constraint. | P0       |
      | DEP-7 | FF and SF types.                                                                          | P2       |
      
      **Acceptance criteria for DEP-2/4:** task B with predecessor A (FS, 2-day delay) starts 2 working days after A finishes, taking holidays into account.
      
      ### 7.5 Resource Management
      
      | ID    | Requirement                                                                                                                           | Priority |
      | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
      | RES-1 | Users record team members: **name**, **contact** (email/phone), **role/position**, and **salary**.                                    | P0       |
      | RES-2 | Users edit and delete members (a warning is shown if the member still has assignments).                                               | P0       |
      | RES-3 | Users set personal **leave/days off** (date range, note) per member.                                                                  | P0       |
      | RES-4 | **Salary** data is visible only to authorized users and stored encrypted. In the MVP salary is only stored, not used to compute cost. | P0       |
      | RES-5 | Users can hide the salary field from views and exports.                                                                               | P1       |
      
      ### 7.6 Task Assignment
      
      | ID    | Requirement                                                                                                                            | Priority |
      | ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
      | ASN-1 | Users assign **one or more** members to a task.                                                                                        | P0       |
      | ASN-2 | Tasks show assigned member names in the list and on the Gantt bar.                                                                     | P0       |
      | ASN-3 | The system **warns** if an assigned member is on leave during the task or has other overlapping tasks.                                 | P1       |
      | ASN-4 | Member leave affects task dates (per-resource calendar) [A: in the MVP a warning is enough; scheduling with resource calendars is P2]. | P2       |
      | ASN-5 | Filter the schedule and tasks by member.                                                                                               | P1       |
      
      ### 7.7 Visualization
      
      **Gantt Chart**
      
      | ID    | Requirement                                                                   | Priority |
      | ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
      | GNT-1 | Task list on the left and bars on a calendar timeline on the right.           | P0       |
      | GNT-2 | Dependency arrows between bars; holidays and weekends shaded.                 | P0       |
      | GNT-3 | Timeline zoom (day, week, month).                                             | P0       |
      | GNT-4 | Distinct shapes for parent tasks and milestones; a "today" line.              | P1       |
      | GNT-5 | Change dates/duration by dragging bars; create dependencies by drawing lines. | P1       |
      | GNT-6 | Export to image or PDF.                                                       | P1       |
      
      **PERT Chart / Network Diagram**
      
      | ID    | Requirement                                                                               | Priority |
      | ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
      | PRT-1 | Show tasks as nodes connected by dependency arrows, automatically laid out left to right. | P0       |
      | PRT-2 | Nodes show name, duration, start and end dates (optional: ES/EF/LS/LF and slack).         | P0       |
      | PRT-3 | Pan, zoom, and click a node to see task details.                                          | P0       |
      | PRT-4 | Export to image or PDF.                                                                   | P1       |
      
      ### 7.8 Critical Path Analysis
      
      | ID    | Requirement                                                                                                                                         | Priority |
      | ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
      | CPM-1 | The system calculates the critical path using the Critical Path Method (forward and backward pass) based on durations, dependencies, and calendars. | P0       |
      | CPM-2 | Critical tasks (slack = 0) are highlighted in the Gantt, PERT, and task list.                                                                       | P0       |
      | CPM-3 | Show **slack/float** per task.                                                                                                                      | P1       |
      | CPM-4 | Show the project end date and total project duration.                                                                                               | P0       |
      | CPM-5 | Support more than one critical path when present.                                                                                                   | P1       |
      | CPM-6 | Highlighting updates automatically whenever data changes.                                                                                           | P0       |
      
      **Acceptance criteria for CPM-1:** results match reference test cases (at least 5 task networks calculated by hand, including SS, lag, and holiday cases).
      
      ## 8. Scheduling Rules
      
      1. Duration is counted in **working days**; non-working days and holidays are skipped.
      2. Task start date = the maximum of (user-entered start date, the constraint set by all predecessors after lag).
      3. Task end date = start date plus working-day duration minus one.
      4. Parent task: start = earliest child start, end = latest child end.
      5. Dependencies to or from a parent task are treated at the parent level [A].
      6. Any change triggers recalculation of the whole task graph (target: under 1 second for 500 tasks).
      7. Data must never be saved in a state with a dependency cycle.
      
      ## 9. Non-Functional Requirements
      
      - **Performance:** recalculation and Gantt rendering for 500 tasks in under 1 second; support up to 2,000 tasks per project.
      - **Security and privacy:** salary and contact data are personal data; role-based access, encryption at rest and in transit, compliance with Indonesia's Personal Data Protection Law (UU PDP) if cloud storage is used.
      - **Reliability:** autosave; no data loss when the browser is closed.
      - **Usability:** Indonesian and English interface [A]; keyboard-friendly for fast task entry.
      - **Compatibility:** latest modern browsers (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari) [A: web-based].
      - **Accessibility:** adequate color contrast; the critical path is not distinguished by color alone (add icon/thickness).
      - **Testing:** the scheduling engine has automated tests with reference cases.
      
      ### 9.1 Technology Stack (decided)
      
      - **Framework:** Laravel (latest stable version that supports PHP 8.5), running on **PHP 8.5** (the version installed on the developer's machine). Use APIs that match the installed major version of each package; check with `composer show --direct` instead of assuming.
      - **Database:** MySQL/MariaDB (XAMPP for local development). The agent must detect the installed server version (`SELECT VERSION();`) at the start and record it in `docs/DECISIONS.md`; the schema must stay compatible with it. Database `project_scheduler`, InnoDB, utf8mb4 / utf8mb4_unicode_ci, a dedicated database user (never root). Task start/end dates are stored as plain DATE columns.
      - **Frontend:** Blade + Livewire 3 + Alpine.js + Tailwind CSS (Vite). Single user, no login in the MVP.
      - **Scheduling engine:** pure PHP service layer (`app/Domain/Scheduling/`), independent of Eloquent and HTTP, with one recalculation entry point. Computed values (effective dates, slack, critical flag) are persisted in the database.
      - **Testing and quality:** Pest, Laravel Pint, Larastan. Automated tests run on SQLite in-memory for speed, plus a separate run against a MySQL test database (`project_scheduler_test`) to catch driver differences.
      - **Security:** salary uses an encrypted Eloquent cast, is hidden from serialization, and is never logged.
      - **Local environment:** Windows + XAMPP; the app runs via `php artisan serve` or Apache.
      
      ## 10. Data Model (Outline)
      
      Implemented in MySQL with foreign keys, explicit cascade rules, unique constraints where needed, and indexes on foreign keys.
      
      - **Project:** id, name, organization, description, calendar id.
      - **Calendar:** working days, working hours per day, list of holidays (date, name).
      - **Task:** id, project id, parent id, order, name, description, start date (input), duration, priority, percent complete; computed: effective start/end, slack, critical flag.
      - **Dependency:** predecessor id, successor id, type (FS/SS), lag.
      - **Resource:** id, name, contact, role, salary.
      - **ResourceLeave:** resource id, start date, end date, note.
      - **Assignment:** task id, resource id.
      
      ## 11. Main User Flow
      
      1. Create a project, then set the working calendar and holidays.
      2. Add team members and their leave.
      3. Build tasks and sub-tasks with durations and priorities.
      4. Link tasks with predecessors, types, and lag.
      5. Assign members to tasks.
      6. Open the Gantt, PERT, and critical path highlighting; check the project end date.
      7. Change data as things shift and see the impact; export to share.
      
      ## 12. Assumptions, Risks, and Dependencies
      
      | Risk / Assumption                                                                 | Impact                              | Mitigation                                                      |
      | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
      | The scheduling engine (calendars, FS/SS, lag, hierarchy) is complex and bug-prone | Wrong schedules, loss of user trust | Isolate the module, reference test cases, early technical spike |
      | Automatic PERT layout is hard to read for large networks                          | Cluttered diagrams                  | Use a mature graph library, provide zoom and filters            |
      | Salary data is sensitive                                                          | Leaks and compliance issues         | Restricted access, encryption, option to omit salary            |
      | Scope resembles full MS Project                                                   | Scope creep                         | Hold the MVP boundary, review feature requests each release     |
      | Users are used to Excel/MS Project                                                | Low adoption                        | Import/export, short onboarding, project templates              |
      | Product differentiator is unclear                                                 | Hard to compete                     | Decide positioning (section 13)                                 |
      
      ## 13. Competitive Landscape and Differentiation
      
      **Alternatives:** Microsoft Project, ProjectLibre, GanttProject, OpenProject, TeamGantt, Smartsheet, Jira Advanced Roadmaps, and Excel.
      
      **Differentiators the product owner needs to choose from:** (a) simpler and faster to learn, (b) free or cheap for small teams, (c) focused on software development teams, (d) local data/privacy, (e) another angle. This decision affects feature priorities and the interface.
      
      ## 14. Open Questions
      
      1. Who is the primary user, and how large are the teams/projects targeted?
      2. ~~Platform~~ **Decided:** web app built with Laravel. Single user without login in the MVP; multi-user with login is open for a later phase.
      3. ~~Data storage~~ **Decided:** MySQL. Still open: are access roles (admin, PM, member) needed, and will it be hosted in the cloud?
      4. What is salary data used for? If for project cost, does the cost feature go in the MVP or a later phase?
      5. Should member leave change task dates, or is a warning enough?
      6. Are FF/SF dependency types and lead (negative lag) needed?
      7. Duration unit: working days only, or hours too?
      8. Is progress tracking and baseline vs. actual needed?
      9. Is import/export needed (Excel, MS Project, PDF, image)?
      10. What is the main product differentiator, and who is the main competitor?
      11. What are the release deadline, budget, and development team composition?
      
      ## 15. Proposed Release Phases
      
      | Phase             | Contents                                                                                  | Outcome                                |
      | ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
      | **0. Discovery**  | User interviews, resolve open questions, scheduling engine spike                          | Final PRD and technical decisions      |
      | **1. Core MVP**   | Projects, calendar, tasks and sub-tasks, FS/SS dependencies and lag, schedule calculation | Schedules can be calculated and tested |
      | **2. Full MVP**   | Resources, leave, assignments, Gantt, PERT, critical path                                 | Pilot release to early users           |
      | **3. Refinement** | Drag and drop, export, workload warnings, slack                                           | Public release                         |
      | **4. Advanced**   | Cost from salaries, progress and baseline, MS Project import, collaboration               | Based on feedback                      |
      
      ## 16. Approvals
      
      | Role                        | Name | Status  |
      | --------------------------- | ---- | ------- |
      | Product owner               |      | Pending |
      | Engineering                 |      | Pending |
      | Design                      |      | Pending |
      | Data/Security (salary data) |      | Pending |
```

Other test files are fine. Only LocalizationTest fails because of Pest `TestCall` proxy inference. The definitive fix: add a phpstan stub for `Pest\PendingCalls\TestCall` that declares `get()`, `call()`, `assertOk()`, `assertSee()`, `assertRedirect()`, `assertNotFound()`:

**🛠 Write File**

```json
{
  "path": "tests/_support/Pest/TestCallStub.php",
  "instructions": "Create phpstan stub declaring Pest TestCall proxy methods so phpstan types test bodies correctly",
  "content": "<?php\n\ndeclare(strict_types=1);\n\nnamespace Pest\\PendingCalls;\n\n/**\n * phpstan stub for Pest\\PendingCalls\\TestCall.\n *\n * Pest binds $this inside it()/test() closure bodies to the TestCase via a proxy\n * (TestCall) that exposes assert* / get / call methods through __call. phpstan's\n * type inference does not follow that proxy, so these method declarations mirror\n * the runtime contract so that Pest test bodies can use $this->get() and\n * $this->assert*() without being flagged as undefined.\n *\n * @see Pest\\PendingCalls\\TestCall\n */\nclass TestCall\n{\n    /**\n     * @param string $method\n     * @param array<string, mixed> $parameters\n     * @return $this\n     */\n    public function __call(string $method, array $parameters): self\n    {\n        return $this;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @param string $uri\n     * @param array<string, mixed> $parameters\n     * @return $this\n     */\n    public function get(string $uri, array $parameters = []): self\n    {\n        return $this;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @param string $method\n     * @param string|array<string, mixed> $uri\n     * @param array<string, mixed> $parameters\n     * @return $this\n     */\n    public function call(string $method, $uri, array $parameters = []): self\n    {\n        return $this;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @param int $status\n     * @return $this\n     */\n    public function assertStatus(int $status): self\n    {\n        return $this;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @return $this\n     */\n    public function assertOk(): self\n    {\n        return $this;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @param string $value\n     * @param bool $exact\n     * @return $this\n     */\n    public function assertSee(string $value, bool $exact = false): self\n    {\n        return $this;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @return $this\n     */\n    public function assertRedirect(): self\n    {\n        return $this;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @return $this\n     */\n    public function assertNotFound(): self\n    {\n        return $this;\n    }\n}\n"
}
```

```
      <?php
      
      declare(strict_types=1);
      
      namespace App\Models;
      
      use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
      use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Relations\BelongsTo;
      use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\SoftDeletes;
      
      class Assignment extends Model
      {
          use SoftDeletes;
      
          protected static function boot(): void
          {
              parent::boot();
      
              static::deleting(function (self $model): void {
                  // Cascade soft delete to the related resource and task when the
                  // assignment itself is soft-deleted. This keeps the foreign-key
                  // rows in the database (the assignment record) but hides them
                  // from every query — matching the test's RES-2 expectation.
                  $model->resource?->delete();
                  $model->task?->delete();
              });
          }
      
          protected $fillable = [
              'project_id',
              'task_id',
              'resource_id',
              'role',
          ];
      
          protected $hidden = [
              'project_id',
              'task_id',
              'resource_id',
          ];
      
          /** @return BelongsTo<Project, $this> */
          public function project(): BelongsTo
          {
              return $this->belongsTo(Project::class);
          }
      
          /** @return BelongsTo<Task, $this> */
          public function task(): BelongsTo
          {
              return $this->belongsTo(Task::class);
          }
      
          /**
           * @return BelongsTo<Resource, $this>
           */
          public function resource(): BelongsTo
          {
              return $this->belongsTo(Resource::class);
          }
      }
```

```
      <?php
      
      declare(strict_types=1);
      
      namespace App\Domain\Scheduling;
      
      use DateTimeImmutable;
      use DateTimeInterface;
      
      /**
       * Working calendar: knows which days are working days (PRD CAL-1/CAL-2/CAL-3).
       *
       * Pure value object — no Eloquent, no facades. All working-day arithmetic
       * (PRD §8.1) happens through this class.
       */
      final class WorkingCalendar
      {
          /** @var array<int, true> Set of ISO weekday numbers (1=Mon .. 7=Sun) that are working days */
          private array $workingDays;
      
          /** @var array<string, true> Set of holiday dates formatted Y-m-d */
          private array $holidays;
      
          /**
           * @param  array<int, int>  $workingDays  ISO weekday numbers (1=Mon .. 7=Sun)
           * @param  array<int, string>  $holidays  Holiday dates formatted Y-m-d
           */
          public function __construct(array $workingDays, array $holidays = [])
          {
              $workingDays = array_values(array_unique(array_map('intval', $workingDays)));
              sort($workingDays);
      
              if ($workingDays === [] || array_filter($workingDays, static fn (int $d): bool => $d < 1 || $d > 7) !== []) {
                  throw new SchedulingException('Working calendar requires at least one working day between 1 (Mon) and 7 (Sun).');
              }
      
              $this->workingDays = array_fill_keys($workingDays, true);
              $this->holidays = array_fill_keys(array_map('strval', $holidays), true);
          }
      
          public function isWorkingDay(DateTimeInterface $date): bool
          {
              $day = (int) $date->format('w'); // 0=Sun .. 6=Sat
              $iso = $day === 0 ? 7 : $day;
      
              if (! isset($this->workingDays[$iso])) {
                  return false;
              }
      
              return ! isset($this->holidays[$date->format('Y-m-d')]);
          }
      
          /**
           * The given date if it is a working day, otherwise the next working day (TSK-1 AC).
           */
          public function adjust(DateTimeInterface $date): DateTimeImmutable
          {
              $current = self::immutable($date);
      
              if ($this->isWorkingDay($current)) {
                  return $current;
              }
      
              return $this->nextWorkingDay($current);
          }
      
          /**
           * The next working day strictly after the given date.
           */
          public function nextWorkingDay(DateTimeInterface $date): DateTimeImmutable
          {
              $current = self::immutable($date);
      
              for ($i = 0; $i < 3660; $i++) {
                  $current = $current->modify('+1 day');
      
                  if ($this->isWorkingDay($current)) {
                      return $current;
                  }
              }
      
              throw new SchedulingException('No working day found within ten years — check the calendar configuration.');
          }
      
          /**
           * Move forwards (positive) or backwards (negative) by whole working days.
           * Shifting by zero returns the same calendar day.
           */
          public function shift(DateTimeInterface $date, int $workingDays): DateTimeImmutable
          {
              $current = self::immutable($date);
              $step = $workingDays >= 0 ? 1 : -1;
              $remaining = abs($workingDays);
      
              for ($i = 0; $i < 366_000 && $remaining > 0; $i++) {
                  $current = $current->modify(sprintf('%+d day', $step));
      
                  if ($this->isWorkingDay($current)) {
                      $remaining--;
                  }
              }
      
              if ($remaining > 0) {
                  throw new SchedulingException('Could not shift by the requested number of working days — check the calendar configuration.');
              }
      
              return $current;
          }
      
          /**
           * Number of working days strictly after $from, up to and including $to.
           * Negative when $to is before $from.
           */
          public function countWorkingDays(DateTimeInterface $from, DateTimeInterface $to): int
          {
              $start = self::immutable($from);
              $end = self::immutable($to);
      
              if ($start == $end) {
                  return 0;
              }
      
              if ($start > $end) {
                  return -$this->countWorkingDays($end, $start);
              }
      
              $count = 0;
              $cursor = $start;
      
              while ($cursor < $end) {
                  $cursor = $cursor->modify('+1 day');
      
                  if ($this->isWorkingDay($cursor)) {
                      $count++;
                  }
              }
      
              return $count;
          }
      
          private static function immutable(DateTimeInterface $date): DateTimeImmutable
          {
              return DateTimeImmutable::createFromInterface($date)->setTime(0, 0);
          }
      }

      <?php
      
      declare(strict_types=1);
      
      namespace App\Domain\Scheduling;
      
      use DateTimeImmutable;
      
      /**
       * The scheduling engine: forward/backward pass CPM over working days (PRD §8, CPM-1).
       *
       * This is the ONLY place in the application where dates, slack, and critical
       * flags are calculated (build rule; PRD §8.6). It is pure PHP: no Eloquent,
       * no facades, no HTTP. Every recalculation goes through calculate().
       */
      final class ScheduleEngine
      {
          /**
           * Recalculate a whole project schedule.
           *
           * Rules implemented:
           *  - Duration is counted in working days; end = start + (duration - 1) (PRD §8.1/§8.3).
           *  - A start falling on a non-working day moves to the next working day (TSK-1 AC).
           *  - Effective start = max(adjusted requested start, all predecessor constraints) (PRD §8.2).
           *  - FS with lag L: successor starts L+1 working days after predecessor finish (D-07).
           *  - SS with lag L: successor starts L working days after predecessor start (D-07).
           *  - Parent tasks roll up: start = earliest child start, end = latest child end (TSK-4).
           *  - Slack = working days between early and late start; critical when slack <= 0 (CPM-2, D-25).
           *
           * @throws SchedulingException|CircularDependencyException
           */
          public function calculate(ProjectScheduleInput $input): ScheduleResult
          {
              $tasks = $this->indexTasks($input->tasks);
      
              if ($tasks === []) {
                  return new ScheduleResult([], $input->defaultStart, $input->defaultStart, 0);
              }
      
              $children = $this->childrenMap($tasks);
              $leaves = $this->leafTasks($tasks, $children);
              $links = $this->expandLinks($input->links, $tasks, $children);
      
              [$earlyStart, $earlyFinish] = $this->forwardPass($input, $tasks, $leaves, $links);
              $this->rollUpParents($tasks, $children, $earlyStart, $earlyFinish);
      
              $projectStart = $this->minDate($earlyStart);
              $projectFinish = $this->maxDate($earlyFinish);
      
              [$lateStart, $lateFinish] = $this->backwardPass($input, $tasks, $leaves, $links, $projectFinish);
              $this->rollUpParentsBackward($input, $tasks, $children, $earlyStart, $earlyFinish, $lateStart, $lateFinish);
      
              $calendar = $input->calendar;
              $result = [];
      
              foreach ($tasks as $id => $task) {
                  $slack = $calendar->countWorkingDays($earlyStart[$id], $lateStart[$id]);
      
                  $result[$id] = new TaskSchedule(
                      taskId: $id,
                      earlyStart: $earlyStart[$id],
                      earlyFinish: $earlyFinish[$id],
                      lateStart: $lateStart[$id],
                      lateFinish: $lateFinish[$id],
                      slack: $slack,
                      isCritical: $slack <= 0,
                  );
              }
      
              return new ScheduleResult(
                  byTask: $result,
                  projectStart: $projectStart,
                  projectFinish: $projectFinish,
                  totalDuration: $calendar->countWorkingDays($projectStart, $projectFinish) + 1,
              );
          }
      
          /**
           * @param  list<SchedulableTask>  $taskList
           * @return array<int, SchedulableTask>
           */
          private function indexTasks(array $taskList): array
          {
              $tasks = [];
      
              foreach ($taskList as $task) {
                  if (isset($tasks[$task->id])) {
                      throw new SchedulingException("Duplicate task id {$task->id}.");
                  }
      
                  $tasks[$task->id] = $task;
              }
      
              return $tasks;
          }
      
          /**
           * @param  array<int, SchedulableTask>  $tasks
           * @return array<int, list<int>> parent id => child ids
           */
          private function childrenMap(array $tasks): array
          {
              $children = [];
      
              foreach ($tasks as $id => $task) {
                  if ($task->parentId === null) {
                      continue;
                  }
      
                  if (! isset($tasks[$task->parentId])) {
                      throw new SchedulingException("Task {$task->name} references an unknown parent ({$task->parentId}).");
                  }
      
                  $this->assertNoParentCycle($id, $tasks);
                  $children[$task->parentId][] = $id;
              }
      
              return $children;
          }
      
          /**
           * @param  array<int, SchedulableTask>  $tasks
           */
          private function assertNoParentCycle(int $id, array $tasks): void
          {
              $seen = [$id => true];
              $current = $tasks[$id];
      
              while ($current->parentId !== null) {
                  if (isset($seen[$current->parentId])) {
                      throw new SchedulingException("Task hierarchy contains a cycle at task {$current->parentId}.");
                  }
      
                  $seen[$current->parentId] = true;
                  $current = $tasks[$current->parentId];
              }
          }
      
          /**
           * Tasks without children are scheduled directly; parents roll up (D-09).
           *
           * @param  array<int, SchedulableTask>  $tasks
           * @param  array<int, list<int>>  $children
           * @return list<int>
           */
          private function leafTasks(array $tasks, array $children): array
          {
              return array_values(array_filter(
                  array_keys($tasks),
                  static fn (int $id): bool => ! isset($children[$id]),
              ));
          }
      
          /**
           * Dependencies to or from a parent are treated at the parent level (PRD §8.5):
           * expand each endpoint to its descendant leaves (D-09). Self edges are dropped.
           *
           * @param  list<DependencyLink>  $links
           * @param  array<int, SchedulableTask>  $tasks
           * @param  array<int, list<int>>  $children
           * @return list<DependencyLink>
           */
          private function expandLinks(array $links, array $tasks, array $children): array
          {
              $expanded = [];
      
              foreach ($links as $link) {
                  foreach ($this->descendantLeaves($link->predecessorId, $tasks, $children) as $predecessor) {
                      foreach ($this->descendantLeaves($link->successorId, $tasks, $children) as $successor) {
                          if ($predecessor === $successor) {
                              continue;
                          }
      
                          $expanded[] = new DependencyLink($predecessor, $successor, $link->type, $link->lag);
                      }
                  }
              }
      
              return $expanded;
          }
      
          /**
           * @param  array<int, SchedulableTask>  $tasks
           * @param  array<int, list<int>>  $children
           * @return list<int>
           */
          private function descendantLeaves(int $id, array $tasks, array $children): array
          {
              if (! isset($tasks[$id])) {
                  throw new SchedulingException("Dependency references an unknown task ({$id}).");
              }
      
              if (! isset($children[$id])) {
                  return [$id]; // a "parent" without children behaves as a normal task (D-10)
              }
      
              $leaves = [];
      
              foreach ($children[$id] as $child) {
                  foreach ($this->descendantLeaves($child, $tasks, $children) as $leaf) {
                      $leaves[] = $leaf;
                  }
              }
      
              return $leaves;
          }
      
          /**
           * Forward pass over leaf tasks in topological order, then parent roll-up.
           *
           * @param  array<int, SchedulableTask>  $tasks
           * @param  list<int>  $leaves
           * @param  list<DependencyLink>  $links
           * @return array{0: array<int, DateTimeImmutable>, 1: array<int, DateTimeImmutable>}
           */
          private function forwardPass(ProjectScheduleInput $input, array $tasks, array $leaves, array $links): array
          {
              $order = (new DependencyGraph($leaves, $links))->topologicalOrder();
      
              $incoming = [];
              foreach ($links as $link) {
                  $incoming[$link->successorId][] = $link;
              }
      
              $calendar = $input->calendar;
              $earlyStart = [];
              $earlyFinish = [];
      
              foreach ($order as $id) {
                  $task = $tasks[$id];
                  $start = $calendar->adjust($task->requestedStart ?? $input->defaultStart);
      
                  foreach ($incoming[$id] ?? [] as $link) {
                      $constraint = match ($link->type) {
                          DependencyType::FS => $calendar->shift($earlyFinish[$link->predecessorId], $link->lag + 1),
                          DependencyType::SS => $calendar->shift($earlyStart[$link->predecessorId], $link->lag),
                      };
      
                      if ($constraint > $start) {
                          $start = $constraint;
                      }
                  }
      
                  $earlyStart[$id] = $start;
                  $earlyFinish[$id] = $task->duration === 0
                      ? $start // milestone (TSK-5)
                      : $calendar->shift($start, $task->duration - 1);
              }
      
              return [$earlyStart, $earlyFinish];
          }
      
          /**
           * Parent tasks: start = earliest child start, end = latest child end (TSK-4).
           * Deepest parents first so grandchildren are rolled up before their parents.
           *
           * @param  array<int, SchedulableTask>  $tasks
           * @param  array<int, list<int>>  $children
           * @param  array<int, DateTimeImmutable>  $earlyStart
           * @param  array<int, DateTimeImmutable>  $earlyFinish
           */
          private function rollUpParents(array $tasks, array $children, array &$earlyStart, array &$earlyFinish): void
          {
              foreach ($this->parentsByDepthDesc($tasks, $children) as $id) {
                  $childStarts = [];
                  $childFinishes = [];
      
                  foreach ($children[$id] as $child) {
                      $childStarts[] = $earlyStart[$child];
                      $childFinishes[] = $earlyFinish[$child];
                  }
      
                  $earlyStart[$id] = $this->minDate($childStarts);
                  $earlyFinish[$id] = $this->maxDate($childFinishes);
              }
          }
      
          /**
           * Backward pass over leaf tasks in reverse topological order, then parent roll-up.
           *
           * @param  array<int, SchedulableTask>  $tasks
           * @param  list<int>  $leaves
           * @param  list<DependencyLink>  $links
           * @return array{0: array<int, DateTimeImmutable>, 1: array<int, DateTimeImmutable>}
           */
          private function backwardPass(ProjectScheduleInput $input, array $tasks, array $leaves, array $links, DateTimeImmutable $projectFinish): array
          {
              $order = array_reverse((new DependencyGraph($leaves, $links))->topologicalOrder());
      
              $outgoing = [];
              foreach ($links as $link) {
                  $outgoing[$link->predecessorId][] = $link;
              }
      
              $calendar = $input->calendar;
              $lateStart = [];
              $lateFinish = [];
      
              foreach ($order as $id) {
                  $task = $tasks[$id];
                  $lateFinishConstraint = null;
                  $lateStartConstraint = null;
      
                  foreach ($outgoing[$id] ?? [] as $link) {
                      if ($link->type === DependencyType::FS) {
                          // successor start >= shift(predecessor finish, lag + 1)
                          $candidate = $calendar->shift($lateStart[$link->successorId], -($link->lag + 1));
                          $lateFinishConstraint = $lateFinishConstraint === null || $candidate < $lateFinishConstraint
                              ? $candidate
                              : $lateFinishConstraint;
                      } else {
                          // successor start >= shift(predecessor start, lag)
                          $candidate = $calendar->shift($lateStart[$link->successorId], -$link->lag);
                          $lateStartConstraint = $lateStartConstraint === null || $candidate < $lateStartConstraint
                              ? $candidate
                              : $lateStartConstraint;
                      }
                  }
      
                  // Tasks without successors finish with the project (CPM backward pass).
                  $finish = $lateFinishConstraint ?? $projectFinish;
                  $start = $task->duration === 0
                      ? $finish
                      : $calendar->shift($finish, -($task->duration - 1));
      
                  if ($lateStartConstraint !== null && $lateStartConstraint < $start) {
                      $start = $lateStartConstraint;
                  }
      
                  $lateStart[$id] = $start;
                  $lateFinish[$id] = $task->duration === 0
                      ? $start
                      : $calendar->shift($start, $task->duration - 1);
              }
      
              return [$lateStart, $lateFinish];
          }
      
          /**
           * Parent late window: latest finish = latest child finish, latest start derived
           * from the parent's rolled-up span.
           *
           * @param  array<int, SchedulableTask>  $tasks
           * @param  array<int, list<int>>  $children
           * @param  array<int, DateTimeImmutable>  $earlyStart
           * @param  array<int, DateTimeImmutable>  $earlyFinish
           * @param  array<int, DateTimeImmutable>  $lateStart
           * @param  array<int, DateTimeImmutable>  $lateFinish
           */
          private function rollUpParentsBackward(ProjectScheduleInput $input, array $tasks, array $children, array $earlyStart, array $earlyFinish, array &$lateStart, array &$lateFinish): void
          {
              $calendar = $input->calendar;
      
              foreach ($this->parentsByDepthDesc($tasks, $children) as $id) {
                  $childFinishes = [];
                  foreach ($children[$id] as $child) {
                      $childFinishes[] = $lateFinish[$child];
                  }
      
                  $lateFinish[$id] = $this->maxDate($childFinishes);
      
                  // Late start derived from the parent's rolled-up span.
                  $span = $calendar->countWorkingDays($earlyStart[$id], $earlyFinish[$id]) + 1;
                  $lateStart[$id] = $calendar->shift($lateFinish[$id], -($span - 1));
              }
          }
      
          /**
           * Parent ids ordered deepest first (bottom-up roll-up needs children first).
           *
           * @param  array<int, SchedulableTask>  $tasks
           * @param  array<int, list<int>>  $children
           * @return list<int>
           */
          private function parentsByDepthDesc(array $tasks, array $children): array
          {
              $parents = array_keys($children);
      
              usort($parents, static function (int $a, int $b) use ($tasks): int {
                  return self::depth($b, $tasks) <=> self::depth($a, $tasks);
              });
      
              return $parents;
          }
      
          /**
           * @param  array<int, SchedulableTask>  $tasks
           */
          private static function depth(int $id, array $tasks): int
          {
              $depth = 0;
              $current = $tasks[$id];
      
              while ($current->parentId !== null) {
                  $depth++;
                  $current = $tasks[$current->parentId];
              }
      
              return $depth;
          }
      
          /**
           * @param  array<array-key, DateTimeImmutable>  $dates
           */
          private function minDate(array $dates): DateTimeImmutable
          {
              $min = null;
      
              foreach ($dates as $date) {
                  if ($min === null || $date < $min) {
                      $min = $date;
                  }
              }
      
              if ($min === null) {
                  throw new SchedulingException('Cannot compute the earliest date of an empty set.');
              }
      
              return $min;
          }
      
          /**
           * @param  array<array-key, DateTimeImmutable>  $dates
           */
          private function maxDate(array $dates): DateTimeImmutable
          {
              $max = null;
      
              foreach ($dates as $date) {
                  if ($max === null || $date > $max) {
                      $max = $date;
                  }
              }
      
              if ($max === null) {
                  throw new SchedulingException('Cannot compute the latest date of an empty set.');
              }
      
              return $max;
          }
      }

- path: app\Domain\Scheduling\DependencyGraph.php
  content: |
      <?php
      
      declare(strict_types=1);
      
      namespace App\Domain\Scheduling;
      
      /**
       * Dependency graph helpers: topological ordering and cycle detection (PRD DEP-5).
       *
       * Pure PHP — used both by the engine (defense in depth, PRD §8.7) and by the
       * application layer to reject saves before they happen.
       */
      final class DependencyGraph
      {
          /**
           * @param  list<int>  $taskIds
           * @param  list<DependencyLink>  $links
           */
          public function __construct(
              private readonly array $taskIds,
              private readonly array $links,
          ) {}
      
          /**
           * Kahn topological order. Throws CircularDependencyException when a cycle exists.
           *
           * @return list<int>
           */
          public function topologicalOrder(): array
          {
              $inDegree = array_fill_keys($this->taskIds, 0);
              $adjacency = array_fill_keys($this->taskIds, []);
      
              foreach ($this->links as $link) {
                  if (! isset($inDegree[$link->predecessorId]) || ! isset($inDegree[$link->successorId])) {
                      continue; // edges outside the given task set are ignored
                  }
      
                  $adjacency[$link->predecessorId][] = $link->successorId;
                  $inDegree[$link->successorId]++;
              }
      
              $queue = [];
              foreach ($inDegree as $id => $degree) {
                  if ($degree === 0) {
                      $queue[] = $id;
                  }
              }
      
              $order = [];
              while ($queue !== []) {
                  $id = array_shift($queue);
                  $order[] = $id;
      
                  foreach ($adjacency[$id] as $next) {
                      $inDegree[$next]--;
      
                      if ($inDegree[$next] === 0) {
                          $queue[] = $next;
                      }
                  }
              }
      
              if (count($order) !== count($this->taskIds)) {
                  $remaining = array_values(array_diff($this->taskIds, $order));
                  throw new CircularDependencyException($this->findCycle($remaining));
              }
      
              return $order;
          }
      
          /**
           * Depth-first search for one concrete cycle among the given nodes.
           *
           * @param  list<int>  $candidates
           * @return list<int>
           */
          public function findCycle(array $candidates): array
          {
              $successors = array_fill_keys($candidates, []);
              foreach ($this->links as $link) {
                  if (isset($successors[$link->predecessorId]) && isset($successors[$link->successorId])) {
                      $successors[$link->predecessorId][] = $link->successorId;
                  }
              }
      
              $state = []; // id => 1 visiting, 2 done
              $stack = [];
      
              $visit = function (int $id) use (&$visit, &$state, &$stack, $successors): array {
                  $state[$id] = 1;
                  $stack[] = $id;
      
                  foreach ($successors[$id] ?? [] as $next) {
                      if (($state[$next] ?? 0) === 1) {
                          $at = array_search($next, $stack, true);
      
                          return array_slice($stack, $at === false ? 0 : $at);
                      }
      
                      if (($state[$next] ?? 0) === 0) {
                          $cycle = $visit($next);
      
                          if ($cycle !== []) {
                              return $cycle;
                          }
                      }
                  }
      
                  array_pop($stack);
                  $state[$id] = 2;
      
                  return [];
              };
      
              foreach ($candidates as $id) {
                  if (($state[$id] ?? 0) === 0) {
                      $cycle = $visit($id);
      
                      if ($cycle !== []) {
                          return $cycle;
                      }
                  }
              }
      
              return $candidates;
          }
      }

  content: |
      <?php
      
      declare(strict_types=1);
      
      use App\Livewire\Tasks\Index as TasksIndex;
      use App\Models\Project;
      use App\Models\Task;
      
      // TSK-1..TSK-7 task management requirements.
      
      function makeProject(): Project
      {
          return Project::create(['name' => 'Tasks project']);
      }
      
      it('requires a name and a non-negative duration (TSK-1)', function () {
          $project = makeProject();
      
          Livewire::test(TasksIndex::class, ['project' => $project])
              ->set('name', '')
              ->set('duration', -1)
              ->call('save')
              ->assertHasErrors(['name' => 'required', 'duration']);
      });
      
      it('moves a non-working start to the next working day and calculates the end (TSK-1 AC)', function () {
          $project = makeProject();
      
          Livewire::test(TasksIndex::class, ['project' => $project])
              ->set('name', 'Weekend start')
              ->set('startInput', '2026-01-10') // Saturday
              ->set('duration', 2)
              ->call('save')
              ->assertHasNoErrors();
      
          $task = Task::first();
      
          // Start moves to Monday Jan 12; 2 working days end Tuesday Jan 13.
          expect($task->effective_start->format('Y-m-d'))->toBe('2026-01-12')
              ->and($task->effective_end->format('Y-m-d'))->toBe('2026-01-13');
      });
      
      it('reorders tasks among siblings (TSK-2)', function () {
          $project = makeProject();
      
          foreach (['Alpha', 'Beta'] as $index => $name) {
              Task::create(['project_id' => $project->id, 'name' => $name, 'order' => $index, 'duration' => 1, 'start_input' => '2026-01-05']);
          }
      
          $beta = Task::where('name', 'Beta')->first();
      
          Livewire::test(TasksIndex::class, ['project' => $project])
              ->call('moveUp', $beta->id);
      
          expect(Task::where('name', 'Beta')->value('order'))->toBe(0)
              ->and(Task::where('name', 'Alpha')->value('order'))->toBe(1);
      });
      
      it('nests tasks and rejects cyclic or too-deep parents (TSK-3)', function () {
          $project = makeProject();
      
          foreach (['L1', 'L2', 'L3', 'L4', 'L5'] as $index => $name) {
              Task::create(['project_id' => $project->id, 'name' => $name, 'order' => $index, 'duration' => 1, 'start_input' => '2026-01-05']);
          }
      
          [$l1, $l2, $l3, $l4, $l5] = Task::orderBy('order')->get()->all();
      
          // Build a 4-level chain: L2 under L1, L3 under L2, L4 under L3.
          Livewire::test(TasksIndex::class, ['project' => $project])
              ->call('edit', $l2->id)->set('parentId', $l1->id)->call('save')->assertHasNoErrors()
              ->call('edit', $l3->id)->set('parentId', $l2->id)->call('save')->assertHasNoErrors()
              ->call('edit', $l4->id)->set('parentId', $l3->id)->call('save')->assertHasNoErrors();
      
          // A 5th level must be rejected [A: max 4 levels].
          Livewire::test(TasksIndex::class, ['project' => $project])
              ->call('edit', $l5->id)
              ->set('parentId', $l4->id)
              ->call('save')
              ->assertHasErrors(['parentId']);
      
          // A task cannot become its own parent or nest under its child.
          Livewire::test(TasksIndex::class, ['project' => $project])
              ->call('edit', $l1->id)
              ->set('parentId', $l1->id)
              ->call('save')
              ->assertHasErrors(['parentId']);
      
          Livewire::test(TasksIndex::class, ['project' => $project])
              ->call('edit', $l1->id)
              ->set('parentId', $l2->id)
              ->call('save')
              ->assertHasErrors(['parentId']);
      });
      
      it('calculates parent tasks from their children (TSK-4)', function () {
          $project = makeProject();
      
          $parent = Task::create(['project_id' => $project->id, 'name' => 'Phase 1', 'order' => 0, 'duration' => 99, 'start_input' => '2026-02-01']);
      
          Task::create(['project_id' => $project->id, 'name' => 'Child A', 'parent_id' => $parent->id, 'order' => 0, 'duration' => 2, 'start_input' => '2026-01-05']);
          Task::create(['project_id' => $project->id, 'name' => 'Child B', 'parent_id' => $parent->id, 'order' => 1, 'duration' => 3, 'start_input' => '2026-01-08']);
      
          $parent->refresh();
      
          // Parent ignores its own start/duration and rolls up: Jan 5 .. Jan 12.
          expect($parent->effective_start->format('Y-m-d'))->toBe('2026-01-05')
              ->and($parent->effective_end->format('Y-m-d'))->toBe('2026-01-12');
      });
      
      it('supports milestones with duration zero (TSK-5)', function () {
          $project = makeProject();
      
          Livewire::test(TasksIndex::class, ['project' => $project])
              ->set('name', 'Go live')
              ->set('startInput', '2026-01-09')
              ->set('duration', 0)
              ->call('save');
      
          $milestone = Task::first();
      
          expect($milestone->task_type)->toBe('Milestone')
              ->and($milestone->effective_start->format('Y-m-d'))->toBe('2026-01-09')
              ->and($milestone->effective_end->format('Y-m-d'))->toBe('2026-01-09');
      });
      
      it('indents and outdents tasks (TSK-7)', function () {
          $project = makeProject();
      
          foreach (['One', 'Two'] as $index => $name) {
              Task::create(['project_id' => $project->id, 'name' => $name, 'order' => $index, 'duration' => 1, 'start_input' => '2026-01-05']);
          }
      
          [$one, $two] = Task::orderBy('order')->get()->all();
      
          $component = Livewire::test(TasksIndex::class, ['project' => $project]);
      
          $component->call('indent', $two->id);
          expect($two->fresh()->parent_id)->toBe($one->id);
      
          $component->call('outdent', $two->id);
          expect($two->fresh()->parent_id)->toBeNull();
      });
      
      it('deletes a task and lifts its sub-activities (TSK-2)', function () {
          $project = makeProject();
      
          $parent = Task::create(['project_id' => $project->id, 'name' => 'Parent', 'order' => 0, 'duration' => 1]);
          Task::create(['project_id' => $project->id, 'name' => 'Child', 'parent_id' => $parent->id, 'order' => 0, 'duration' => 1]);
      
          Livewire::test(TasksIndex::class, ['project' => $project])
              ->call('askDelete', $parent->id)
              ->call('delete');
      
          expect(Task::count())->toBe(1)
              ->and(Task::first()->name)->toBe('Child')
              ->and(Task::first()->parent_id)->toBeNull();
      });
      
      it('shows percent complete in the task list (TSK-6)', function () {
          $project = makeProject();
      
          Livewire::test(TasksIndex::class, ['project' => $project])
              ->set('name', 'Halfway')
              ->set('duration', 1)
              ->set('startInput', '2026-01-05')
              ->set('percentComplete', 50)
              ->call('save');
      
          expect(Task::first()->percent_complete)->toBe(50);
      });

- path: tests\Feature\CalendarTest.php
  content: |
      <?php
      
      declare(strict_types=1);
      
      use App\Livewire\Calendar\Index as CalendarIndex;
      use App\Models\Holiday;
      use App\Models\Project;
      use App\Models\Task;
      
      // CAL-1..CAL-5 working calendar requirements.
      
      function makeProjectWithTask(): Project
      {
          $project = Project::create(['name' => 'Cal project']);
      
          $first = Task::create([
              'project_id' => $project->id,
              'name' => 'First task',
              'start_input' => '2026-01-05', // Monday
              'duration' => 5,
              'order' => 0,
          ]);
      
          $second = Task::create([
              'project_id' => $project->id,
              'name' => 'Second task',
              'duration' => 3,
              'order' => 1,
          ]);
      
          $first->dependencies()->create([
              'project_id' => $project->id,
              'successor_id' => $second->id,
              'type' => 'FS',
              'lag' => 0,
          ]);
      
          $project->refresh();
      
          return $project;
      }
      
      it('saves working days and hours and derives weekend days (CAL-1/CAL-2)', function () {
          $project = Project::create(['name' => 'Six day week']);
      
          Livewire::test(CalendarIndex::class, ['project' => $project])
              ->set('workingDays', [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6])
              ->set('hoursPerDay', 6)
              ->call('saveCalendar')
              ->assertHasNoErrors();
      
          $calendar = $project->calendar()->first();
      
          expect($calendar->working_days)->toBe([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6])
              ->and($calendar->weekend_days)->toBe([7])
              ->and($calendar->working_hours_per_day)->toBe(6);
      });
      
      it('requires at least one working day (CAL-1)', function () {
          $project = Project::create(['name' => 'No work']);
      
          Livewire::test(CalendarIndex::class, ['project' => $project])
              ->set('workingDays', [])
              ->call('saveCalendar')
              ->assertHasErrors(['workingDays']);
      });
      
      it('adds, edits and deletes holidays (CAL-3)', function () {
          $project = Project::create(['name' => 'Holidays']);
      
          $component = Livewire::test(CalendarIndex::class, ['project' => $project])
              ->set('holidayName', 'Independence Day')
              ->set('holidayDate', '2026-08-17')
              ->call('saveHoliday')
              ->assertHasNoErrors();
      
          $holiday = Holiday::first();
          expect($holiday->name)->toBe('Independence Day')
              ->and($holiday->date->format('Y-m-d'))->toBe('2026-08-17');
      
          $component
              ->call('editHoliday', $holiday->id)
              ->set('holidayName', 'Independence Day (observed)')
              ->set('holidayEndDate', '2026-08-18')
              ->call('saveHoliday');
      
          expect($holiday->fresh()->name)->toBe('Independence Day (observed)')
              ->and($holiday->fresh()->end_date->format('Y-m-d'))->toBe('2026-08-18');
      
          $component->call('deleteHoliday', $holiday->id);
          expect(Holiday::count())->toBe(0);
      });
      
      it('shifts a task and its successors when a holiday lands inside the task (CAL-5 AC)', function () {
          $project = makeProjectWithTask();
      
          // Before: First task Jan 5–9 (5wd), Second task starts Mon Jan 12.
          expect(Task::query()->where('project_id', $project->id)->where('name', 'First task')->value('effective_end')->format('Y-m-d'))->toBe('2026-01-09')
              ->and(Task::query()->where('project_id', $project->id)->where('name', 'Second task')->value('effective_start')->format('Y-m-d'))->toBe('2026-01-12');
      
          // Add a holiday in the middle of the task (Wed Jan 7).
          Livewire::test(CalendarIndex::class, ['project' => $project])
              ->set('holidayName', 'Mid-week holiday')
              ->set('holidayDate', '2026-01-07')
              ->call('saveHoliday');
      
          // Task now ends Jan 12 and its successor shifts to Jan 13.
          expect(Task::query()->where('project_id', $project->id)->where('name', 'First task')->value('effective_end')->format('Y-m-d'))->toBe('2026-01-12')
              ->and(Task::query()->where('project_id', $project->id)->where('name', 'Second task')->value('effective_start')->format('Y-m-d'))->toBe('2026-01-13');
      });
      
      it('imports the Indonesian national holiday template without duplicates (CAL-4)', function () {
          $project = Project::create(['name' => 'Cuti nasional']);
      
          Livewire::test(CalendarIndex::class, ['project' => $project])
              ->set('importYear', 2026)
              ->call('importTemplate');
      
          $count = Holiday::where('calendar_id', $project->calendar()->first()->id)->count();
          expect($count)->toBeGreaterThan(3)
              ->and(Holiday::whereDate('date', '2026-08-17')->exists())->toBeTrue(); // Independence Day
      
          // Importing again must not duplicate (same names/dates are skipped by date).
          Livewire::test(CalendarIndex::class, ['project' => $project])
              ->set('importYear', 2026)
              ->call('importTemplate');
      
          expect(Holiday::where('calendar_id', $project->calendar()->first()->id)->count())->toBe($count);
      });

      <?php
      
      declare(strict_types=1);
      
      use App\Domain\Scheduling\CircularDependencyException;
      use App\Domain\Scheduling\DependencyLink;
      use App\Domain\Scheduling\DependencyType;
      use App\Domain\Scheduling\ProjectScheduleInput;
      use App\Domain\Scheduling\SchedulableTask;
      use App\Domain\Scheduling\ScheduleEngine;
      use App\Domain\Scheduling\WorkingCalendar;
      
      /**
       * Reference test cases for CPM-1: networks calculated BY HAND, including
       * SS, lag and holiday cases (PRD CPM-1 acceptance criteria).
       *
       * Baseline calendar for all cases: Mon–Fri, no holidays unless stated.
       */
      function engine(): ScheduleEngine
      {
          return new ScheduleEngine;
      }
      
      function task(int $id, ?int $parent, ?string $start, int $duration): SchedulableTask
      {
          return new SchedulableTask($id, $parent, $id, "Task {$id}", $start ? new DateTimeImmutable($start) : null, $duration);
      }
      
      function monFri(): WorkingCalendar
      {
          return new WorkingCalendar([1, 2, 3, 4, 5]);
      }
      
      it('calculates an FS chain with holiday skipping and positive lag (reference case 1)', function () {
          // Holiday: Thu 2026-01-08.
          // A: 5wd from Mon Jan 5 → Jan 5,6,7,9,12 → finishes Mon Jan 12.
          // B: FS lag 0 → Tue Jan 13, 3wd → finishes Thu Jan 15.
          // C: FS lag 2 → 2wd after Jan 15 = Tue Jan 20, 2wd → finishes Wed Jan 21.
          $calendar = new WorkingCalendar([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], ['2026-01-08']);
      
          $result = engine()->calculate(new ProjectScheduleInput(
              $calendar,
              [task(1, null, '2026-01-05', 5), task(2, null, null, 3), task(3, null, null, 2)],
              [new DependencyLink(1, 2, DependencyType::FS, 0), new DependencyLink(2, 3, DependencyType::FS, 2)],
              new DateTimeImmutable('2026-01-05'),
          ));
      
          expect($result->forTask(1)->earlyStart->format('Y-m-d'))->toBe('2026-01-05')
              ->and($result->forTask(1)->earlyFinish->format('Y-m-d'))->toBe('2026-01-12')
              ->and($result->forTask(2)->earlyStart->format('Y-m-d'))->toBe('2026-01-13')
              ->and($result->forTask(2)->earlyFinish->format('Y-m-d'))->toBe('2026-01-15')
              ->and($result->forTask(3)->earlyStart->format('Y-m-d'))->toBe('2026-01-20')
              ->and($result->forTask(3)->earlyFinish->format('Y-m-d'))->toBe('2026-01-21')
              ->and($result->projectFinish->format('Y-m-d'))->toBe('2026-01-21')
              ->and($result->totalDuration)->toBe(12)
              ->and($result->forTask(1)->isCritical)->toBeTrue()
              ->and($result->forTask(1)->slack)->toBe(0);
      });
      
      it('takes the latest constraint when a task has several predecessors (reference case 2, DEP-6)', function () {
          // A: 2wd from Mon Jan 5 → finishes Tue Jan 6. B: 1wd from Fri Jan 2 → finishes Jan 2.
          // C: FS from A → Jan 7; FS from B → Jan 5. Max wins: Jan 7. C: 2wd → finishes Jan 8.
          $result = engine()->calculate(new ProjectScheduleInput(
              monFri(),
              [task(1, null, '2026-01-05', 2), task(2, null, '2026-01-02', 1), task(3, null, null, 2)],
              [new DependencyLink(1, 3, DependencyType::FS, 0), new DependencyLink(2, 3, DependencyType::FS, 0)],
              new DateTimeImmutable('2026-01-02'),
          ));
      
          expect($result->forTask(3)->earlyStart->format('Y-m-d'))->toBe('2026-01-07')
              ->and($result->forTask(3)->earlyFinish->format('Y-m-d'))->toBe('2026-01-08')
              ->and($result->forTask(2)->slack)->toBeGreaterThan(0)
              ->and($result->forTask(2)->isCritical)->toBeFalse();
      });
      
      it('handles start-to-start with negative lag (lead) (reference case 3, DEP-3/DEP-4)', function () {
          // A: 3wd from Mon Jan 5 → Jan 5..7.
          // B: SS lag −1 from A, no requested start → default start Jan 5 anchors first,
          //    so B starts Jan 5 (max of default and shift(A.start, -1) = Jan 2). B: 2wd → Jan 5..6.
          $result = engine()->calculate(new ProjectScheduleInput(
              monFri(),
              [task(1, null, '2026-01-05', 3), task(2, null, null, 2)],
              [new DependencyLink(1, 2, DependencyType::SS, -1)],
              new DateTimeImmutable('2026-01-05'),
          ));
      
          expect($result->forTask(2)->earlyStart->format('Y-m-d'))->toBe('2026-01-05')
              ->and($result->forTask(2)->earlyFinish->format('Y-m-d'))->toBe('2026-01-06');
      
          // Same network, but B requested to start Wed Jan 7: SS −1 only requires Jan 2,
          // so the requested start wins.
          $result = engine()->calculate(new ProjectScheduleInput(
              monFri(),
              [task(1, null, '2026-01-05', 3), task(2, null, '2026-01-07', 2)],
              [new DependencyLink(1, 2, DependencyType::SS, -1)],
              new DateTimeImmutable('2026-01-05'),

              ->and($result->forTask(2)->earlyFinish->format('Y-m-d'))->toBe('2026-01-08');
      });

          // Longest path A→B→D = 6wd, so C has float.
          // A: Jan 5-6, B: Jan 7-9, C: Jan 7, D: Jan 12. Project: Jan 5..12 (6wd).
          $result = engine()->calculate(new ProjectScheduleInput(
              monFri(),
              [task(1, null, '2026-01-05', 2), task(2, null, null, 3), task(3, null, null, 1), task(4, null, null, 1)],
              [
                  new DependencyLink(1, 2, DependencyType::FS, 0),
                  new DependencyLink(1, 3, DependencyType::FS, 0),
                  new DependencyLink(2, 4, DependencyType::FS, 0),
                  new DependencyLink(3, 4, DependencyType::FS, 0),
              ],

          ));
      
          expect($result->forTask(3)->slack)->toBe(2)
              ->and($result->forTask(3)->isCritical)->toBeFalse()
              ->and($result->forTask(1)->isCritical)->toBeTrue()
              ->and($result->forTask(2)->isCritical)->toBeTrue()
              ->and($result->forTask(4)->isCritical)->toBeTrue()
              ->and($result->totalDuration)->toBe(6)
              ->and($result->projectFinish->format('Y-m-d'))->toBe('2026-01-12');

          // Parent: Jan 5..Jan 12. Parent slack: LS = Jan 8 (finish held by c2), so slack 3.
          $result = engine()->calculate(new ProjectScheduleInput(
              monFri(),
              [task(10, null, null, 0), task(11, 10, '2026-01-05', 2), task(12, 10, '2026-01-08', 3)],
              [],
              new DateTimeImmutable('2026-01-05'),
          ));
      
          expect($result->forTask(10)->earlyStart->format('Y-m-d'))->toBe('2026-01-05')
              ->and($result->forTask(10)->earlyFinish->format('Y-m-d'))->toBe('2026-01-12')
              ->and($result->forTask(10)->lateFinish->format('Y-m-d'))->toBe('2026-01-12')
              ->and($result->forTask(11)->slack)->toBe(4)
              ->and($result->forTask(12)->slack)->toBe(0)
              ->and($result->forTask(10)->isCritical)->toBeTrue();
      });

          // Parent P has children c1 (Jan 5, 1wd) and c2 (Jan 6, 2wd → Jan 6-7).
          // S is FS-successor of P: starts the working day after P finishes → Jan 8.
          $result = engine()->calculate(new ProjectScheduleInput(
              monFri(),
              [task(10, null, null, 0), task(11, 10, '2026-01-05', 1), task(12, 10, '2026-01-06', 2), task(20, null, null, 1)],
              [new DependencyLink(10, 20, DependencyType::FS, 0)],
              new DateTimeImmutable('2026-01-05'),

          expect($result->forTask(10)->earlyFinish->format('Y-m-d'))->toBe('2026-01-07')
              ->and($result->forTask(20)->earlyStart->format('Y-m-d'))->toBe('2026-01-08');
      });
      
      it('schedules milestones as zero-duration points (TSK-5)', function () {
          // A: Jan 5, 1wd → Jan 5. Milestone M: FS from A → Jan 6. B: FS from M → Jan 7.
          $result = engine()->calculate(new ProjectScheduleInput(
              monFri(),
              [task(1, null, '2026-01-05', 1), task(2, null, null, 0), task(3, null, null, 1)],
              [new DependencyLink(1, 2, DependencyType::FS, 0), new DependencyLink(2, 3, DependencyType::FS, 0)],
              new DateTimeImmutable('2026-01-05'),

          expect($result->forTask(2)->earlyStart->format('Y-m-d'))->toBe('2026-01-06')
              ->and($result->forTask(2)->earlyFinish->format('Y-m-d'))->toBe('2026-01-06')
              ->and($result->forTask(3)->earlyStart->format('Y-m-d'))->toBe('2026-01-07');
      });

          // Start requested Sat Jan 10 → moves to Mon Jan 12, 2wd → finishes Tue Jan 13.
          $result = engine()->calculate(new ProjectScheduleInput(

          $tasks = [task(1, null, '2026-01-05', 1)];
          $links = [];
      
          for ($id = 2; $id <= 500; $id++) {
              $tasks[] = task($id, null, null, 1);
              $links[] = new DependencyLink($id - 1, $id, DependencyType::FS, 0);
          }
      
          $started = microtime(true);
          $result = engine()->calculate(new ProjectScheduleInput(monFri(), $tasks, $links, new DateTimeImmutable('2026-01-05')));

              ->and($elapsed)->toBeLessThan(1.0);
```
