# PRD: Project Scheduling Application for Development Teams

**Status:** Draft 0.1 | **Owner:** (TBD) | **Date:** October 9, 2026

> This draft is based on an initial feature description. Anything not yet known is written as an **assumption** (marked [A]) or an **open question** (section 14) so it can be validated before development begins.

## 1. Summary

An application for building, calculating, and visualizing software project schedules. Users create a project, structure tasks hierarchically with dependencies, set up working calendars and team member leave, and then view the result as a Gantt Chart, a PERT/Network Diagram, and a critical path. The system automatically calculates task dates from durations, dependencies, and calendars.

## 2. Background and Problem Statement

Project managers and tech leads of development teams struggle to build and track realistic schedules because task dependencies, holidays, and team availability must be calculated manually (usually in spreadsheets). As a result, schedules are error-prone, hard to update when things change, and delay risk (the critical path) stays invisible.

**Supporting evidence:** none yet. Needs to be gathered through interviews with 5-8 PMs/tech leads and samples of the schedules they use today (see section 14).

## 3. Goals and Non-Goals

### Goals

1. Speed up creation of an initial project schedule compared with manual methods.
2. Produce correct task dates automatically from dependencies and calendars.
3. Make the critical path clearly visible so delay risks can be anticipated.
4. Provide a visual overview of the schedule (Gantt and PERT) that is easy to share.

### Non-Goals (first version)

- Project cost/budget calculation from salaries.
- Automatic resource leveling.
- Real-time multi-user collaboration.
- Time tracking and timesheets.
- Third-party integrations (Jira, Slack, etc.).

## 4. Users and Scenarios

| Persona                                   | Description                                     | Key needs                                                                  |
| ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Project Manager / Tech Lead** (primary) | Builds and maintains software project schedules | Build schedules quickly, see the impact of changes, find the critical path |
| **Team member** [A]                       | Task recipient                                  | View their tasks and schedule (read-only in v1)                            |
| **Stakeholder** [A]                       | Management/client                               | View a schedule summary via export                                         |

**Primary scenario:** A PM creates a new project, sets the working calendar, enters tasks and sub-tasks, links them with dependencies, assigns team members, then opens the Gantt chart and critical path to check whether the deadline is achievable. When a task slips or a member goes on leave, the PM changes the data and sees the schedule recalculated.

## 5. Success Metrics

| Metric                                                                                                      | Baseline               | Target (proposed)                 |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| Time to build an initial schedule for a 50-task project                                                     | Measure current method | At least 50% reduction            |
| Correctness of date and critical path calculations                                                          | -                      | 100% pass on reference test cases |
| Users who build a complete schedule (project with tasks, dependencies, assignments) within the first 7 days | -                      | 40%                               |
| Projects whose schedule is updated more than once                                                           | -                      | 50%                               |
| User satisfaction (SUS or short survey)                                                                     | -                      | Score of 70 or higher             |

Baselines and targets need to be validated with the product owner.

## 6. Scope

**In scope (MVP):** all modules in section 7, with FS and SS dependencies, one calendar per project, per-member leave calendars, Gantt, PERT, and critical path.

**Deferred:** cost from salaries, FF/SF, resource leveling, advanced baseline and progress tracking, notifications, real-time collaboration, MS Project import, mobile app.

## 7. Functional Requirements

Priority: **P0** required for MVP, **P1** should have, **P2** later.

### 7.1 Project Management

| ID    | Requirement                                                                                   | Priority |
| ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| PRJ-1 | Users can create a project with a **name** (required), **organization**, and **description**. | P0       |
| PRJ-2 | Users can view the project list, open, edit, and delete projects (with confirmation).         | P0       |
| PRJ-3 | Users can duplicate a project as a template.                                                  | P2       |

**Acceptance criteria for PRJ-1:** an empty name is rejected with a clear message; the project is saved and appears in the list; a default calendar is created automatically.

### 7.2 Working Calendar

| ID    | Requirement                                                                                               | Priority |
| ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| CAL-1 | Users define the **working days** per week and working hours per day [A: default Monday-Friday, 8 hours]. | P0       |
| CAL-2 | Users define **weekend** days that are excluded from calculations.                                        | P0       |
| CAL-3 | Users add, edit, and delete **custom/national holidays** (date, name, optional date range).               | P0       |
| CAL-4 | Import the Indonesian national holiday list as a template.                                                | P1       |
| CAL-5 | Any calendar change triggers recalculation of the whole schedule.                                         | P0       |

**Acceptance criteria for CAL-5:** after adding a holiday in the middle of a task's range, the task's end date shifts accordingly and successor tasks shift with it.

### 7.3 Task Management

| ID    | Requirement                                                                                                                               | Priority |
| ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| TSK-1 | Users add tasks with a **name**, **start date**, **duration** (working days), and **priority** (Low/Medium/High/Critical).                | P0       |
| TSK-2 | Users edit, delete, and reorder tasks.                                                                                                    | P0       |
| TSK-3 | **Sub-activities:** tasks can be nested under a parent task (hierarchy up to [A] 4 levels).                                               | P0       |
| TSK-4 | Parent tasks are calculated automatically from their children (earliest start to latest finish); parent duration is not entered manually. | P0       |
| TSK-5 | **Milestone** task type (duration 0).                                                                                                     | P1       |
| TSK-6 | Additional fields: description, percent complete.                                                                                         | P1       |
| TSK-7 | Indent/outdent to change task level, and copy/paste tasks.                                                                                | P1       |

**Acceptance criteria for TSK-1:** duration must be a positive number; a start date falling on a non-working day is automatically moved to the next working day; the end date is calculated from duration and calendar.

### 7.4 Task Dependencies

| ID    | Requirement                                                                               | Priority |
| ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| DEP-1 | Users set one or more **predecessors** on a task.                                         | P0       |
| DEP-2 | **Finish-to-Start (FS)**: the task starts after its predecessor finishes.                 | P0       |
| DEP-3 | **Start-to-Start (SS)**: the task starts together with or after its predecessor starts.   | P0       |
| DEP-4 | **Delay/lag** in working days between tasks (negative lag/lead allowed [A]).              | P0       |
| DEP-5 | The system **prevents circular dependencies** and shows a message identifying the cycle.  | P0       |
| DEP-6 | When a task has several predecessors, its start date is taken from the latest constraint. | P0       |
| DEP-7 | FF and SF types.                                                                          | P2       |

**Acceptance criteria for DEP-2/4:** task B with predecessor A (FS, 2-day delay) starts 2 working days after A finishes, taking holidays into account.

### 7.5 Resource Management

| ID    | Requirement                                                                                                                           | Priority |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| RES-1 | Users record team members: **name**, **contact** (email/phone), **role/position**, and **salary**.                                    | P0       |
| RES-2 | Users edit and delete members (a warning is shown if the member still has assignments).                                               | P0       |
| RES-3 | Users set personal **leave/days off** (date range, note) per member.                                                                  | P0       |
| RES-4 | **Salary** data is visible only to authorized users and stored encrypted. In the MVP salary is only stored, not used to compute cost. | P0       |
| RES-5 | Users can hide the salary field from views and exports.                                                                               | P1       |

### 7.6 Task Assignment

| ID    | Requirement                                                                                                                            | Priority |
| ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| ASN-1 | Users assign **one or more** members to a task.                                                                                        | P0       |
| ASN-2 | Tasks show assigned member names in the list and on the Gantt bar.                                                                     | P0       |
| ASN-3 | The system **warns** if an assigned member is on leave during the task or has other overlapping tasks.                                 | P1       |
| ASN-4 | Member leave affects task dates (per-resource calendar) [A: in the MVP a warning is enough; scheduling with resource calendars is P2]. | P2       |
| ASN-5 | Filter the schedule and tasks by member.                                                                                               | P1       |

### 7.7 Visualization

**Gantt Chart**

| ID    | Requirement                                                                   | Priority |
| ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| GNT-1 | Task list on the left and bars on a calendar timeline on the right.           | P0       |
| GNT-2 | Dependency arrows between bars; holidays and weekends shaded.                 | P0       |
| GNT-3 | Timeline zoom (day, week, month).                                             | P0       |
| GNT-4 | Distinct shapes for parent tasks and milestones; a "today" line.              | P1       |
| GNT-5 | Change dates/duration by dragging bars; create dependencies by drawing lines. | P1       |
| GNT-6 | Export to image or PDF.                                                       | P1       |

**PERT Chart / Network Diagram**

| ID    | Requirement                                                                               | Priority |
| ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| PRT-1 | Show tasks as nodes connected by dependency arrows, automatically laid out left to right. | P0       |
| PRT-2 | Nodes show name, duration, start and end dates (optional: ES/EF/LS/LF and slack).         | P0       |
| PRT-3 | Pan, zoom, and click a node to see task details.                                          | P0       |
| PRT-4 | Export to image or PDF.                                                                   | P1       |

### 7.8 Critical Path Analysis

| ID    | Requirement                                                                                                                                         | Priority |
| ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| CPM-1 | The system calculates the critical path using the Critical Path Method (forward and backward pass) based on durations, dependencies, and calendars. | P0       |
| CPM-2 | Critical tasks (slack = 0) are highlighted in the Gantt, PERT, and task list.                                                                       | P0       |
| CPM-3 | Show **slack/float** per task.                                                                                                                      | P1       |
| CPM-4 | Show the project end date and total project duration.                                                                                               | P0       |
| CPM-5 | Support more than one critical path when present.                                                                                                   | P1       |
| CPM-6 | Highlighting updates automatically whenever data changes.                                                                                           | P0       |

**Acceptance criteria for CPM-1:** results match reference test cases (at least 5 task networks calculated by hand, including SS, lag, and holiday cases).

## 8. Scheduling Rules

1. Duration is counted in **working days**; non-working days and holidays are skipped.
2. Task start date = the maximum of (user-entered start date, the constraint set by all predecessors after lag).
3. Task end date = start date plus working-day duration minus one.
4. Parent task: start = earliest child start, end = latest child end.
5. Dependencies to or from a parent task are treated at the parent level [A].
6. Any change triggers recalculation of the whole task graph (target: under 1 second for 500 tasks).
7. Data must never be saved in a state with a dependency cycle.

## 9. Non-Functional Requirements

- **Performance:** recalculation and Gantt rendering for 500 tasks in under 1 second; support up to 2,000 tasks per project.
- **Security and privacy:** salary and contact data are personal data; role-based access, encryption at rest and in transit, compliance with Indonesia's Personal Data Protection Law (UU PDP) if cloud storage is used.
- **Reliability:** autosave; no data loss when the browser is closed.
- **Usability:** Indonesian and English interface [A]; keyboard-friendly for fast task entry.
- **Compatibility:** latest modern browsers (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari) [A: web-based].
- **Accessibility:** adequate color contrast; the critical path is not distinguished by color alone (add icon/thickness).
- **Testing:** the scheduling engine has automated tests with reference cases.

### 9.1 Technology Stack (decided)

- **Framework:** Laravel (latest stable version that supports PHP 8.5), running on **PHP 8.5** (the version installed on the developer's machine). Use APIs that match the installed major version of each package; check with `composer show --direct` instead of assuming.
- **Database:** MySQL/MariaDB (XAMPP for local development). The agent must detect the installed server version (`SELECT VERSION();`) at the start and record it in `docs/DECISIONS.md`; the schema must stay compatible with it. Database `project_scheduler`, InnoDB, utf8mb4 / utf8mb4_unicode_ci, a dedicated database user (never root). Task start/end dates are stored as plain DATE columns.
- **Frontend:** Blade + Livewire 3 + Alpine.js + Tailwind CSS (Vite). Single user, no login in the MVP.
- **Scheduling engine:** pure PHP service layer (`app/Domain/Scheduling/`), independent of Eloquent and HTTP, with one recalculation entry point. Computed values (effective dates, slack, critical flag) are persisted in the database.
- **Testing and quality:** Pest, Laravel Pint, Larastan. Automated tests run on SQLite in-memory for speed, plus a separate run against a MySQL test database (`project_scheduler_test`) to catch driver differences.
- **Security:** salary uses an encrypted Eloquent cast, is hidden from serialization, and is never logged.
- **Local environment:** Windows + XAMPP; the app runs via `php artisan serve` or Apache.

## 10. Data Model (Outline)

Implemented in MySQL with foreign keys, explicit cascade rules, unique constraints where needed, and indexes on foreign keys.

- **Project:** id, name, organization, description, calendar id.
- **Calendar:** working days, working hours per day, list of holidays (date, name).
- **Task:** id, project id, parent id, order, name, description, start date (input), duration, priority, percent complete; computed: effective start/end, slack, critical flag.
- **Dependency:** predecessor id, successor id, type (FS/SS), lag.
- **Resource:** id, name, contact, role, salary.
- **ResourceLeave:** resource id, start date, end date, note.
- **Assignment:** task id, resource id.

## 11. Main User Flow

1. Create a project, then set the working calendar and holidays.
2. Add team members and their leave.
3. Build tasks and sub-tasks with durations and priorities.
4. Link tasks with predecessors, types, and lag.
5. Assign members to tasks.
6. Open the Gantt, PERT, and critical path highlighting; check the project end date.
7. Change data as things shift and see the impact; export to share.

## 12. Assumptions, Risks, and Dependencies

| Risk / Assumption                                                                 | Impact                              | Mitigation                                                      |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The scheduling engine (calendars, FS/SS, lag, hierarchy) is complex and bug-prone | Wrong schedules, loss of user trust | Isolate the module, reference test cases, early technical spike |
| Automatic PERT layout is hard to read for large networks                          | Cluttered diagrams                  | Use a mature graph library, provide zoom and filters            |
| Salary data is sensitive                                                          | Leaks and compliance issues         | Restricted access, encryption, option to omit salary            |
| Scope resembles full MS Project                                                   | Scope creep                         | Hold the MVP boundary, review feature requests each release     |
| Users are used to Excel/MS Project                                                | Low adoption                        | Import/export, short onboarding, project templates              |
| Product differentiator is unclear                                                 | Hard to compete                     | Decide positioning (section 13)                                 |

## 13. Competitive Landscape and Differentiation

**Alternatives:** Microsoft Project, ProjectLibre, GanttProject, OpenProject, TeamGantt, Smartsheet, Jira Advanced Roadmaps, and Excel.

**Differentiators the product owner needs to choose from:** (a) simpler and faster to learn, (b) free or cheap for small teams, (c) focused on software development teams, (d) local data/privacy, (e) another angle. This decision affects feature priorities and the interface.

# PRD: Project Scheduling Application for Development Teams

**Status:** Draft 0.1 | **Owner:** (TBD) | **Date:** October 9, 2026

> This draft is based on an initial feature description. Anything not yet known is written as an **assumption** (marked [A]) or an **open question** (section 14) so it can be validated before development begins.

## 1. Summary

An application for building, calculating, and visualizing software project schedules. Users create a project, structure tasks hierarchically with dependencies, set up working calendars and team member leave, and then view the result as a Gantt Chart, a PERT/Network Diagram, and a critical path. The system automatically calculates task dates from durations, dependencies, and calendars.

## 2. Background and Problem Statement

Project managers and tech leads of development teams struggle to build and track realistic schedules because task dependencies, holidays, and team availability must be calculated manually (usually in spreadsheets). As a result, schedules are error-prone, hard to update when things change, and delay risk (the critical path) stays invisible.

**Supporting evidence:** none yet. Needs to be gathered through interviews with 5-8 PMs/tech leads and samples of the schedules they use today (see section 14).

## 3. Goals and Non-Goals

### Goals
1. Speed up creation of an initial project schedule compared with manual methods.
2. Produce correct task dates automatically from dependencies and calendars.
3. Make the critical path clearly visible so delay risks can be anticipated.
4. Provide a visual overview of the schedule (Gantt and PERT) that is easy to share.

### Non-Goals (first version)
- Project cost/budget calculation from salaries.
- Automatic resource leveling.
- Real-time multi-user collaboration.
- Time tracking and timesheets.
- Third-party integrations (Jira, Slack, etc.).

## 4. Users and Scenarios

| Persona | Description | Key needs |
|---|---|---|
| **Project Manager / Tech Lead** (primary) | Builds and maintains software project schedules | Build schedules quickly, see the impact of changes, find the critical path |
| **Team member** [A] | Task recipient | View their tasks and schedule (read-only in v1) |
| **Stakeholder** [A] | Management/client | View a schedule summary via export |

**Primary scenario:** A PM creates a new project, sets the working calendar, enters tasks and sub-tasks, links them with dependencies, assigns team members, then opens the Gantt chart and critical path to check whether the deadline is achievable. When a task slips or a member goes on leave, the PM changes the data and sees the schedule recalculated.

## 5. Success Metrics

| Metric | Baseline | Target (proposed) |
|---|---|---|
| Time to build an initial schedule for a 50-task project | Measure current method | At least 50% reduction |
| Correctness of date and critical path calculations | - | 100% pass on reference test cases |
| Users who build a complete schedule (project with tasks, dependencies, assignments) within the first 7 days | - | 40% |
| Projects whose schedule is updated more than once | - | 50% |
| User satisfaction (SUS or short survey) | - | Score of 70 or higher |

Baselines and targets need to be validated with the product owner.

## 6. Scope

**In scope (MVP):** all modules in section 7, with FS and SS dependencies, one calendar per project, per-member leave calendars, Gantt, PERT, and critical path.

**Deferred:** cost from salaries, FF/SF, resource leveling, advanced baseline and progress tracking, notifications, real-time collaboration, MS Project import, mobile app.

## 7. Functional Requirements

Priority: **P0** required for MVP, **P1** should have, **P2** later.

### 7.1 Project Management

| ID | Requirement | Priority |
|---|---|---|
| PRJ-1 | Users can create a project with a **name** (required), **organization**, and **description**. | P0 |
| PRJ-2 | Users can view the project list, open, edit, and delete projects (with confirmation). | P0 |
| PRJ-3 | Users can duplicate a project as a template. | P2 |

**Acceptance criteria for PRJ-1:** an empty name is rejected with a clear message; the project is saved and appears in the list; a default calendar is created automatically.

### 7.2 Working Calendar

| ID | Requirement | Priority |
|---|---|---|
| CAL-1 | Users define the **working days** per week and working hours per day [A: default Monday-Friday, 8 hours]. | P0 |
| CAL-2 | Users define **weekend** days that are excluded from calculations. | P0 |
| CAL-3 | Users add, edit, and delete **custom/national holidays** (date, name, optional date range). | P0 |
| CAL-4 | Import the Indonesian national holiday list as a template. | P1 |
| CAL-5 | Any calendar change triggers recalculation of the whole schedule. | P0 |

**Acceptance criteria for CAL-5:** after adding a holiday in the middle of a task's range, the task's end date shifts accordingly and successor tasks shift with it.

### 7.3 Task Management

| ID | Requirement | Priority |
|---|---|---|
| TSK-1 | Users add tasks with a **name**, **start date**, **duration** (working days), and **priority** (Low/Medium/High/Critical). | P0 |
| TSK-2 | Users edit, delete, and reorder tasks. | P0 |
| TSK-3 | **Sub-activities:** tasks can be nested under a parent task (hierarchy up to [A] 4 levels). | P0 |
| TSK-4 | Parent tasks are calculated automatically from their children (earliest start to latest finish); parent duration is not entered manually. | P0 |
| TSK-5 | **Milestone** task type (duration 0). | P1 |
| TSK-6 | Additional fields: description, percent complete. | P1 |
| TSK-7 | Indent/outdent to change task level, and copy/paste tasks. | P1 |

**Acceptance criteria for TSK-1:** duration must be a positive number; a start date falling on a non-working day is automatically moved to the next working day; the end date is calculated from duration and calendar.

### 7.4 Task Dependencies

| ID | Requirement | Priority |
|---|---|---|
| DEP-1 | Users set one or more **predecessors** on a task. | P0 |
| DEP-2 | **Finish-to-Start (FS)**: the task starts after its predecessor finishes. | P0 |
| DEP-3 | **Start-to-Start (SS)**: the task starts together with or after its predecessor starts. | P0 |
| DEP-4 | **Delay/lag** in working days between tasks (negative lag/lead allowed [A]). | P0 |
| DEP-5 | The system **prevents circular dependencies** and shows a message identifying the cycle. | P0 |
| DEP-6 | When a task has several predecessors, its start date is taken from the latest constraint. | P0 |
| DEP-7 | FF and SF types. | P2 |

**Acceptance criteria for DEP-2/4:** task B with predecessor A (FS, 2-day delay) starts 2 working days after A finishes, taking holidays into account.

### 7.5 Resource Management

| ID | Requirement | Priority |
|---|---|---|
| RES-1 | Users record team members: **name**, **contact** (email/phone), **role/position**, and **salary**. | P0 |
| RES-2 | Users edit and delete members (a warning is shown if the member still has assignments). | P0 |
| RES-3 | Users set personal **leave/days off** (date range, note) per member. | P0 |
| RES-4 | **Salary** data is visible only to authorized users and stored encrypted. In the MVP salary is only stored, not used to compute cost. | P0 |
| RES-5 | Users can hide the salary field from views and exports. | P1 |

### 7.6 Task Assignment

| ID | Requirement | Priority |
|---|---|---|
| ASN-1 | Users assign **one or more** members to a task. | P0 |
| ASN-2 | Tasks show assigned member names in the list and on the Gantt bar. | P0 |
| ASN-3 | The system **warns** if an assigned member is on leave during the task or has other overlapping tasks. | P1 |
| ASN-4 | Member leave affects task dates (per-resource calendar) [A: in the MVP a warning is enough; scheduling with resource calendars is P2]. | P2 |
| ASN-5 | Filter the schedule and tasks by member. | P1 |

### 7.7 Visualization

**Gantt Chart**

| ID | Requirement | Priority |
|---|---|---|
| GNT-1 | Task list on the left and bars on a calendar timeline on the right. | P0 |
| GNT-2 | Dependency arrows between bars; holidays and weekends shaded. | P0 |
| GNT-3 | Timeline zoom (day, week, month). | P0 |
| GNT-4 | Distinct shapes for parent tasks and milestones; a "today" line. | P1 |
| GNT-5 | Change dates/duration by dragging bars; create dependencies by drawing lines. | P1 |
| GNT-6 | Export to image or PDF. | P1 |

**PERT Chart / Network Diagram**

| ID | Requirement | Priority |
|---|---|---|
| PRT-1 | Show tasks as nodes connected by dependency arrows, automatically laid out left to right. | P0 |
| PRT-2 | Nodes show name, duration, start and end dates (optional: ES/EF/LS/LF and slack). | P0 |
| PRT-3 | Pan, zoom, and click a node to see task details. | P0 |
| PRT-4 | Export to image or PDF. | P1 |

### 7.8 Critical Path Analysis

| ID | Requirement | Priority |
|---|---|---|
| CPM-1 | The system calculates the critical path using the Critical Path Method (forward and backward pass) based on durations, dependencies, and calendars. | P0 |
| CPM-2 | Critical tasks (slack = 0) are highlighted in the Gantt, PERT, and task list. | P0 |
| CPM-3 | Show **slack/float** per task. | P1 |
| CPM-4 | Show the project end date and total project duration. | P0 |
| CPM-5 | Support more than one critical path when present. | P1 |
| CPM-6 | Highlighting updates automatically whenever data changes. | P0 |

**Acceptance criteria for CPM-1:** results match reference test cases (at least 5 task networks calculated by hand, including SS, lag, and holiday cases).

## 8. Scheduling Rules

1. Duration is counted in **working days**; non-working days and holidays are skipped.
2. Task start date = the maximum of (user-entered start date, the constraint set by all predecessors after lag).
3. Task end date = start date plus working-day duration minus one.
4. Parent task: start = earliest child start, end = latest child end.
5. Dependencies to or from a parent task are treated at the parent level [A].
6. Any change triggers recalculation of the whole task graph (target: under 1 second for 500 tasks).
7. Data must never be saved in a state with a dependency cycle.

## 9. Non-Functional Requirements

- **Performance:** recalculation and Gantt rendering for 500 tasks in under 1 second; support up to 2,000 tasks per project.
- **Security and privacy:** salary and contact data are personal data; role-based access, encryption at rest and in transit, compliance with Indonesia's Personal Data Protection Law (UU PDP) if cloud storage is used.
- **Reliability:** autosave; no data loss when the browser is closed.
- **Usability:** Indonesian and English interface [A]; keyboard-friendly for fast task entry.
- **Compatibility:** latest modern browsers (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari) [A: web-based].
- **Accessibility:** adequate color contrast; the critical path is not distinguished by color alone (add icon/thickness).
- **Testing:** the scheduling engine has automated tests with reference cases.

## 10. Data Model (Outline)

- **Project:** id, name, organization, description, calendar id.
- **Calendar:** working days, working hours per day, list of holidays (date, name).
- **Task:** id, project id, parent id, order, name, description, start date (input), duration, priority, percent complete; computed: effective start/end, slack, critical flag.
- **Dependency:** predecessor id, successor id, type (FS/SS), lag.
- **Resource:** id, name, contact, role, salary.
- **ResourceLeave:** resource id, start date, end date, note.
- **Assignment:** task id, resource id.

## 11. Main User Flow

1. Create a project, then set the working calendar and holidays.
2. Add team members and their leave.
3. Build tasks and sub-tasks with durations and priorities.
4. Link tasks with predecessors, types, and lag.
5. Assign members to tasks.
6. Open the Gantt, PERT, and critical path highlighting; check the project end date.
7. Change data as things shift and see the impact; export to share.

## 12. Assumptions, Risks, and Dependencies

| Risk / Assumption | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| The scheduling engine (calendars, FS/SS, lag, hierarchy) is complex and bug-prone | Wrong schedules, loss of user trust | Isolate the module, reference test cases, early technical spike |
| Automatic PERT layout is hard to read for large networks | Cluttered diagrams | Use a mature graph library, provide zoom and filters |
| Salary data is sensitive | Leaks and compliance issues | Restricted access, encryption, option to omit salary |
| Scope resembles full MS Project | Scope creep | Hold the MVP boundary, review feature requests each release |
| Users are used to Excel/MS Project | Low adoption | Import/export, short onboarding, project templates |
| Product differentiator is unclear | Hard to compete | Decide positioning (section 13) |

## 13. Competitive Landscape and Differentiation

**Alternatives:** Microsoft Project, ProjectLibre, GanttProject, OpenProject, TeamGantt, Smartsheet, Jira Advanced Roadmaps, and Excel.

**Differentiators the product owner needs to choose from:** (a) simpler and faster to learn, (b) free or cheap for small teams, (c) focused on software development teams, (d) local data/privacy, (e) another angle. This decision affects feature priorities and the interface.

## 14. Open Questions

1. Who is the primary user, and how large are the teams/projects targeted?
2. Platform: web, desktop, or both? Single user or multi-user with login?
3. Is data stored locally or in the cloud? Are access roles (admin, PM, member) needed?
4. What is salary data used for? If for project cost, does the cost feature go in the MVP or a later phase?
5. Should member leave change task dates, or is a warning enough?
6. Are FF/SF dependency types and lead (negative lag) needed?
7. Duration unit: working days only, or hours too?
8. Is progress tracking and baseline vs. actual needed?
9. Is import/export needed (Excel, MS Project, PDF, image)?
10. What is the main product differentiator, and who is the main competitor?
11. What are the release deadline, budget, and development team composition?

## 15. Proposed Release Phases

| Phase | Contents | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| **0. Discovery** | User interviews, resolve open questions, scheduling engine spike | Final PRD and technical decisions |
| **1. Core MVP** | Projects, calendar, tasks and sub-tasks, FS/SS dependencies and lag, schedule calculation | Schedules can be calculated and tested |
| **2. Full MVP** | Resources, leave, assignments, Gantt, PERT, critical path | Pilot release to early users |
| **3. Refinement** | Drag and drop, export, workload warnings, slack | Public release |
| **4. Advanced** | Cost from salaries, progress and baseline, MS Project import, collaboration | Based on feedback |

# Decision & Assumption Log

Every assumption [A] and non-obvious decision made while building the app per `docs/PRD.md` is logged here.

| # | Area | Decision / Assumption | Rationale |
|---|------|----------------------|-----------|
| D-01 | Docs | The PRD was moved from the repo root (`PRD-Project-Scheduling-App.md`) to `docs/PRD.md` | The build prompt says "Build the app in docs/PRD.md"; PRD is the source of truth |
| D-02 | Stack | Prompt requests "Livewire 3"; installed `livewire/livewire ^4.4` (latest stable compatible with Laravel 13) | Livewire 3 does not support Laravel 13; v4 keeps the same component API for everything used here (Alpine included). Can pin `^3` if an older Laravel is used later |
| D-03 | Database | MySQL database `project_scheduler`, charset `utf8mb4`, engine InnoDB; dedicated user `project_scheduler`@`localhost` (never root), credentials only in `.env` (gitignored) | Prompt requirement; XAMPP MariaDB 10.4 confirmed available |
| D-04 | Tests | Default test run uses SQLite `:memory:` (`phpunit.xml`); `composer test:mysql` runs the same suite on MySQL via `phpunit.mysql.xml`, which overrides only `DB_CONNECTION`/`DB_DATABASE` — credentials come from `.env` | Prompt requirement |
| D-05 | Engine | Scheduling engine lives in `app/Domain/Scheduling/`: pure PHP value objects + `ScheduleEngine::calculate()` as the **one** recalculation entry point. No Eloquent, facades, HTTP, or `Illuminate` imports anywhere in that namespace | Prompt rule + PRD §8.6 |
| D-06 | Engine | Working-day math: ISO weekdays 1 (Mon) – 7 (Sun). Duration counted in working days; task end = start + (duration − 1) working days. A start date on a non-working day is moved forward to the next working day (TSK-1 AC) | PRD §8.1–8.3 |
| D-07 | Engine | Dependency semantics: FS with lag L ⇒ successor starts `L + 1` working days after predecessor's finish (L = 0 ⇒ next working day; L = 2 ⇒ two working days after finish, per DEP-2/4 AC). SS with lag L ⇒ successor starts `L` working days after predecessor's start. Negative lag (lead) allowed; FS lag −1 means starting the same day the predecessor finishes | PRD DEP-2/3/4 + [A] negative lag |
| D-08 | Engine | Multiple predecessors: effective start = max of (adjusted requested start, all predecessor constraints) (DEP-6) | PRD §8.2 |
| D-09 | Engine | Parent (summary) tasks are never scheduled directly: start = earliest child start, end = latest child end (TSK-4). Dependencies pointing **to or from** a parent are expanded to all descendant leaf tasks (PRD §8.5 [A]) — mathematically identical to constraining against the parent's window | Keeps forward/backward passes leaf-only and cycle-free |
| D-10 | Engine | A task flagged/used as a parent but currently having **no children** is treated as a normal task (defensive default) | Avoids empty-window ambiguity |
| D-11 | Engine | Default start for a task without `start_input`: the earliest requested start among project tasks; if none exists, today's date (then adjusted to a working day) | Deterministic and matches the primary scenario (PRD §11) |
| D-12 | Engine | Slack = working days between early start and late start; critical ⇔ slack = 0. Multiple critical paths fall out automatically (CPM-5). Parent slack derives from min child late finish | CPM standard; PRD CPM-2/3/5 |
| D-13 | Integrity | Circular dependencies are rejected at the application layer before save with a message naming the cycle (DEP-5), and the engine additionally throws if fed a cyclic graph (defense in depth, PRD §8.7). DB enforces FKs, unique predecessor→successor pair, and CHECK-style enum domains; app validation mirrors all of it | Prompt rule "integrity in both DB constraints and application validation" |
| D-14 | Recalc | Any change to projects, calendars, holidays, tasks, or dependencies triggers a full-project recalculation (CAL-5, CPM-6, PRD §8.6) via Eloquent observers + explicit calls from UI actions; writes use quiet updates to avoid recursion. All scheduling values are persisted (`effective_*`, `early_*`, `late_*`, `slack`, `is_critical`) so views only read | Single entry point; views never compute dates |
| D-15 | Calendar | One calendar per project, auto-created on project creation (PRJ-1 AC) with defaults [A]: Mon–Fri working, 8 h/day, Sat/Sun weekend. `weekend_days` is derived from working days (stored for display). Holidays live in the `holidays` table (date + optional end date, CAL-3); the legacy `calendars.holidays` JSON column is kept in sync but the table is the source of truth | PRD CAL-1/2/3 |
| D-16 | Salary | `resources.salary` uses the `encrypted:integer` cast, is in `$hidden` (never serialized to JSON), is never logged, and is only stored — not used for cost (RES-4, PRD §3 Non-Goals). Migration column widened from bigint to `text` because encrypted values are ciphertext strings | Prompt rule + PRD |
| D-17 | Salary | RES-5 (hide salary from views): implemented as a session-scoped UI preference toggle on the resources page (no login in MVP, so no per-user DB setting) | Prompt: no login in MVP |
| D-18 | Scope | P1 items that would require **new third-party dependencies** are not built (prompt: "Do not add dependencies without asking"): PDF/image export (GNT-6, PRT-4) and drag-to-edit Gantt (GNT-5). Ideas recorded in `docs/SUGGESTIONS.md` | Prompt rule overrides PRD priority |
| D-19 | Scope | CAL-4 (Indonesian national holiday import) ships as a curated static **template** of well-known national holidays (fixed-date observances + July 17, 2026 substitute for Aug 17 falling on Saturday); clearly labelled "verify against the official SKB list" before use | PRD asks for a template, not guaranteed-official dates |
| D-20 | Scope | TSK-7: indent/outdent buttons are implemented; copy/paste of tasks is deferred to `docs/SUGGESTIONS.md` (no-dep simple version is possible but low value vs. risk; PRD P1) | Scope control |
| D-21 | Locale | UI language: English + Indonesian via `resources/lang/{en,id}/app.php`; switcher stores choice in session; default `en` [A] | PRD §9, prompt |
| D-22 | Data | Priority stored as the PRD labels `Low/Medium/High/Critical`; milestones are `duration = 0` (TSK-5); percent complete 0–100 (TSK-6) | PRD |
| D-23 | Seed | Only fake seed data (`DatabaseSeeder`, "Website Redesign" / Acme Corp, fake people). No real personal data | Prompt rule |
| D-24 | Viz | Gantt and PERT are rendered as server-side SVG computed in Livewire component PHP (layout geometry only — all dates/slack/critical flags come from persisted engine output). No charting library added | Prompt: no JS scheduling logic, no unapproved deps |

# Suggestions (ideas not built)

Ideas parked here per the build prompt ("Put ideas in docs/SUGGESTIONS.md"). None of these are implemented; each needs a product-owner decision (some need new dependencies — the prompt forbids adding dependencies without asking).

## Visualization / P1 items blocked by the no-new-dependency rule

- **GNT-6 / PRT-4 — Export Gantt/PERT to image or PDF.** Add `barryvdh/laravel-dompdf` or `spatie/image` + `spatie/laravel-pdf`, or render SVG → canvas client-side.
- **GNT-5 — Drag bars to change dates/duration; draw dependency lines.** Evaluate `frappe/gantt`, `bryntum/scheduler`, or custom Alpine pointer-events on the existing SVG.

## Scheduling engine

- **FF / SF dependency types (DEP-7, P2).** The engine's constraint model extends naturally; add enum cases + backward-pass rules + tests.
- **Resource leveling / ASN-4 (P2):** per-resource calendars so leave actually shifts dates instead of only warning.
- **Baseline vs. actual + progress tracking (deferred):** store baseline snapshots per project; compare against current calc.
- **Hours-based durations (open question 7)** instead of working days only.
- **Calendar exceptions per task** (e.g., overtime workdays).

## Product / UX

- **Autosave (NFR reliability):** Livewire `wire:model.live` already gives near-realtime saves; add explicit draft recovery + unsaved-changes guard.
- **Project templates / duplication (PRJ-3, P2).**
- **MS Project / Excel import (deferred).**
- **Login, roles, RBAC (open question 2/3):** PM vs. read-only member vs. stakeholder; salary visible only to PM/admin.
- **Notifications** for schedule slips or upcoming leave.
- **Keyboard-first task entry** (NFR usability): shortcuts for add/indent/link.
- **Stakeholder read-only share link** for the Gantt summary.

## Engineering

- **Performance harness:** seeded 500- and 2,000-task projects with a benchmark test asserting the <1 s recalculation target (PRD §9).
- **Mutation testing** (infection) for the scheduling engine — it is the trust-critical module.
- **Queue recalculation** for very large projects (dispatch `RecalculateSchedule` job) once auth/queue infra exists.

<?php

use Illuminate\Support\Str;

return [

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Default Session Driver
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | This option determines the default session driver that is utilized for
    | incoming requests. Laravel supports a variety of storage options to
    | persist session data. Database storage is a great default choice.
    |
    | Supported: "file", "cookie", "database", "memcached",
    |            "redis", "dynamodb", "array"
    |
    */

    'driver' => env('SESSION_DRIVER', 'database'),

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Session Lifetime
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | Here you may specify the number of minutes that you wish the session
    | to be allowed to remain idle before it expires. If you want them
    | to expire immediately when the browser is closed then you may
    | indicate that via the expire_on_close configuration option.
    |
    */

    'lifetime' => (int) env('SESSION_LIFETIME', 120),

    'expire_on_close' => env('SESSION_EXPIRE_ON_CLOSE', false),

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Session Encryption
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | This option allows you to easily specify that all of your session data
    | should be encrypted before it's stored. All encryption is performed
    | automatically by Laravel and you may use the session like normal.
    |
    */

    'encrypt' => env('SESSION_ENCRYPT', false),

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Session File Location
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | When utilizing the "file" session driver, the session files are placed
    | on disk. The default storage location is defined here; however, you
    | are free to provide another location where they should be stored.
    |
    */

    'files' => storage_path('framework/sessions'),

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Session Database Connection
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | When using the "database" or "redis" session drivers, you may specify a
    | connection that should be used to manage these sessions. This should
    | correspond to a connection in your database configuration options.
    |
    */

    'connection' => env('SESSION_CONNECTION'),

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Session Database Table
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | When using the "database" session driver, you may specify the table to
    | be used to store sessions. Of course, a sensible default is defined
    | for you; however, you're welcome to change this to another table.
    |
    */

    'table' => env('SESSION_TABLE', 'sessions'),

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Session Cache Store
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | When using one of the framework's cache driven session backends, you may
    | define the cache store which should be used to store the session data
    | between requests. This must match one of your defined cache stores.
    |
    | Affects: "dynamodb", "memcached", "redis"
    |
    */

    'store' => env('SESSION_STORE'),

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Session Sweeping Lottery
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | Some session drivers must manually sweep their storage location to get
    | rid of old sessions from storage. Here are the chances that it will
    | happen on a given request. By default, the odds are 2 out of 100.
    |
    */

    'lottery' => [2, 100],

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Session Cookie Name
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | Here you may change the name of the session cookie that is created by
    | the framework. Typically, you should not need to change this value
    | since doing so does not grant a meaningful security improvement.
    |
    */

    'cookie' => env(
        'SESSION_COOKIE',
        Str::slug((string) env('APP_NAME', 'laravel')).'-session'
    ),

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Session Cookie Path
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | The session cookie path determines the path for which the cookie will
    | be regarded as available. Typically, this will be the root path of
    | your application, but you're free to change this when necessary.
    |
    */

    'path' => env('SESSION_PATH', '/'),

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Session Cookie Domain
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | This value determines the domain and subdomains the session cookie is
    | available to. By default, the cookie will be available to the root
    | domain without subdomains. Typically, this shouldn't be changed.
    |
    */

    'domain' => env('SESSION_DOMAIN'),

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | HTTPS Only Cookies
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | By setting this option to true, session cookies will only be sent back
    | to the server if the browser has a HTTPS connection. This will keep
    | the cookie from being sent to you when it can't be done securely.
    |
    */

    'secure' => env('SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE'),

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | HTTP Access Only
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | Setting this value to true will prevent JavaScript from accessing the
    | value of the cookie and the cookie will only be accessible through
    | the HTTP protocol. It's unlikely you should disable this option.
    |
    */

    'http_only' => env('SESSION_HTTP_ONLY', true),

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Same-Site Cookies
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | This option determines how your cookies behave when cross-site requests
    | take place, and can be used to mitigate CSRF attacks. By default, we
    | will set this value to "lax" to permit secure cross-site requests.
    |
    | See: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Set-Cookie#samesitesamesite-value
    |
    | Supported: "lax", "strict", "none", null
    |
    */

    'same_site' => env('SESSION_SAME_SITE', 'lax'),

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Partitioned Cookies
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | Setting this value to true will tie the cookie to the top-level site for
    | a cross-site context. Partitioned cookies are accepted by the browser
    | when flagged "secure" and the Same-Site attribute is set to "none".
    |
    */

    'partitioned' => env('SESSION_PARTITIONED_COOKIE', false),

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Session Serialization
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | This value controls the serialization strategy for session data, which
    | is JSON by default. Setting this to "php" allows the storage of PHP
    | objects in the session but can make an application vulnerable to
    | "gadget chain" serialization attacks if the APP_KEY is leaked.
    |
    | Supported: "json", "php"
    |
    */

    'serialization' => 'json',

];

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Livewire\Tasks;

use App\Models\Assignment;
use App\Models\Dependency;
use App\Models\Project;
use App\Models\Resource;
use App\Models\Task;
use App\Services\Schedule\DependencyValidator;
use Illuminate\Contracts\View\View;
use Illuminate\Support\Collection;
use Livewire\Attributes\Layout;
use Livewire\Attributes\Validate;
use Livewire\Component;

/**
 * TSK-1..TSK-4 (P0): tasks with name/start/duration/priority, edit, delete,
 * reorder, nesting up to 4 levels [A], parents calculated from children.
 * P1: milestones (duration 0), percent complete, indent/outdent (TSK-7).
 * DEP-1..DEP-6: predecessors with FS/SS + lag, cycle prevention with a message
 * naming the cycle. ASN-1/ASN-2: assignments shown in the list.
 */
#[Layout('components.layouts.app')]
class Index extends Component
{
    public Project $project;

    // Task form state
    public bool $showModal = false;

    public ?int $editingId = null;

    #[Validate('required|string|max:255')]
    public string $name = '';

    #[Validate('nullable|string|max:2000')]
    public string $description = '';

    #[Validate('nullable|date')]
    public ?string $startInput = null;

    #[Validate('required|integer|min:0|max:3650')]
    public int $duration = 1;

    #[Validate('required|in:Low,Medium,High,Critical')]
    public string $priority = 'Medium';

    #[Validate('required|integer|min:0|max:100')]
    public int $percentComplete = 0;

    public ?int $parentId = null;

    /** @var list<int> */
    public array $assignedResourceIds = [];

    // Predecessor quick-add (DEP-1..DEP-4)
    /** @var array{task_id: int|string|null, type: string, lag: int|string} */
    public array $newPredecessor = ['task_id' => null, 'type' => 'FS', 'lag' => 0];

    /** @var list<string> */
    public array $dependencyErrors = [];

    public ?int $deleteId = null;

    /** ASN-5: filter the schedule by member */
    public ?int $memberFilter = null;

    public function create(): void
    {
        $this->resetForm();
        $this->showModal = true;
    }

    public function edit(int $taskId): void
    {
        $task = $this->findTask($taskId);

        $this->editingId = $task->id;
        $this->name = $task->name;
        $this->description = (string) $task->description;
        $this->startInput = $task->start_input?->format('Y-m-d');
        $this->duration = $task->duration;
        $this->priority = $task->priority;
        $this->percentComplete = $task->percent_complete;
        $this->parentId = $task->parent_id;
        $this->assignedResourceIds = $task->assignments()->pluck('resource_id')->map('intval')->all();
        $this->reset(['newPredecessor', 'dependencyErrors']);
        $this->showModal = true;
    }

    public function save(): void
    {
        $this->validate();

        $data = [
            'project_id' => $this->project->id,
            'name' => $this->name,
            'description' => $this->description ?: null,
            'start_input' => $this->startInput ?: null,
            'duration' => $this->duration,
            'priority' => $this->priority,
            'percent_complete' => $this->percentComplete,
            'parent_id' => $this->parentId,
        ];

        if ($this->editingId === null) {
            $data['order'] = (int) $this->project->tasks()->whereNull('parent_id')->max('order') + 1;
            $task = Task::create($data);
        } else {
            $task = $this->findTask($this->editingId);
            $validator = app(DependencyValidator::class);

            if (
                $task->parent_id !== null
                && $validator->depthOf($task->parent_id, $this->project) + 1 >= 4
            ) {
                $this->addError('parentId', __('tasks.errors.parent_depth'));

                return;
            }

            $task->update($data);
            $this->syncDescendantsTypes($task);
        }

        $task->refresh();
        $this->syncTaskType($task);

        // ASN-1: sync the member list. Hard-delete first: soft-deleted rows
        // would still occupy the unique (task_id, resource_id) index and make
        // re-adding a kept member throw an integrity violation.
        Assignment::query()->where('task_id', $task->id)->forceDelete();
        foreach (array_unique($this->assignedResourceIds) as $resourceId) {
            $resource = Resource::query()
                ->where('project_id', $this->project->id)
                ->find($resourceId);

            if ($resource !== null) {
                Assignment::create([
                    'project_id' => $this->project->id,
                    'task_id' => $task->id,
                    'resource_id' => $resource->id,
                    'role' => $resource->role,
                ]);
            }
        }

        $this->showModal = false;
        $this->resetForm();
    }

    public function askDelete(int $taskId): void
    {
        $this->deleteId = $taskId;
    }

    public function cancelDelete(): void
    {
        $this->deleteId = null;
    }

    public function delete(): void
    {
        if ($this->deleteId === null) {
            return;
        }

        $task = $this->findTask((int) $this->deleteId);

        // Sub-activities are unparented (FK nullOnDelete), dependencies and
        // assignments are soft-deleted explicitly (FK cascades only fire on
        // hard delete), then the observer recalculates the schedule (DEP-5).
        $task->children()->update(['parent_id' => null]);
        Dependency::query()
            ->where('project_id', $this->project->id)
            ->where(static function ($query) use ($task): void {
                $query->where('predecessor_id', $task->id)->orWhere('successor_id', $task->id);
            })
            ->delete();
        Assignment::query()->where('task_id', $task->id)->delete();
        $task->delete();

        $this->deleteId = null;
    }

    public function moveUp(int $taskId): void
    {
        $this->move($taskId, -1);
    }

    public function moveDown(int $taskId): void
    {
        $this->move($taskId, 1);
    }

    /**
     * TSK-7: indent = make the task a child of its previous sibling.
     */
    public function indent(int $taskId): void
    {
        $task = $this->findTask($taskId);
        $siblings = $this->siblingsOf($task);
        $index = $siblings->search(static fn (Task $sibling): bool => $sibling->id === $taskId);

        if ($index === false || $index === 0) {
            return;
        }

        $newParent = $siblings[$index - 1];

        if (app(DependencyValidator::class)->depthOf($newParent->id, $this->project) + 1 >= 4) {
            session()->now('warning', __('tasks.errors.parent_depth'));

            return;
        }

        $task->update(['parent_id' => $newParent->id, 'order' => (int) $this->project->tasks()->where('parent_id', $newParent->id)->max('order') + 1]);
        $this->syncTaskType($task);
    }

    /**
     * TSK-7: outdent = move the task up to its grandparent level.
     */
    public function outdent(int $taskId): void
    {
        $task = $this->findTask($taskId);

        if ($task->parent_id === null) {
            return;
        }

        $parent = $this->findTask($task->parent_id);

        $task->update([
            'parent_id' => $parent->parent_id,
            'order' => (int) $this->project->tasks()->where('parent_id', $parent->parent_id)->max('order') + 1,
        ]);

        $this->syncTaskType($task);
        $this->syncTaskType($parent);
    }

    /**
     * DEP-5: adding a predecessor runs cycle detection first and shows a
     * message identifying the cycle.
     */
    public function addPredecessor(): void
    {
        $this->dependencyErrors = [];

        if ($this->editingId === null || $this->newPredecessor['task_id'] === null) {
            $this->dependencyErrors[] = __('tasks.errors.pred_missing');

            return;
        }

        $predecessor = $this->findTask((int) $this->newPredecessor['task_id']);
        $successor = $this->findTask($this->editingId);
        $type = (string) $this->newPredecessor['type'];
        $lag = (int) $this->newPredecessor['lag'];

        $errors = app(DependencyValidator::class)
            ->validateDependency($this->project, $predecessor, $successor, $type, $lag);

        if ($this->newPredecessor['lag'] !== '' && filter_var($this->newPredecessor['lag'], FILTER_VALIDATE_INT) === false) {
            $errors[] = __('tasks.errors.lag_integer');
        }

        if ($lag < -366 || $lag > 366) {
            $errors[] = __('tasks.errors.lag_bounds');
        }

        if ($errors !== []) {
            $this->dependencyErrors = $errors;

            return;
        }

        $existing = Dependency::query()
            ->where('project_id', $this->project->id)
            ->where('predecessor_id', $predecessor->id)
            ->where('successor_id', $successor->id)
            ->first();

        if ($existing !== null) {
            $this->dependencyErrors[] = __('tasks.errors.pred_exists');

            return;
        }

        Dependency::create([
            'project_id' => $this->project->id,
            'predecessor_id' => $predecessor->id,
            'successor_id' => $successor->id,
            'type' => in_array($type, ['FS', 'SS'], true) ? $type : 'FS',
            'lag' => $lag,
        ]);

        $this->reset('newPredecessor');
        $this->newPredecessor = ['task_id' => null, 'type' => 'FS', 'lag' => 0];
    }

    public function removePredecessor(int $dependencyId): void
    {
        Dependency::query()
            ->where('project_id', $this->project->id)
            ->where('successor_id', $this->editingId)
            ->findOrFail($dependencyId)
            ->delete();
    }

    private function move(int $taskId, int $direction): void
    {
        $task = $this->findTask($taskId);
        $siblings = $this->siblingsOf($task);
        $index = $siblings->search(static fn (Task $sibling): bool => $sibling->id === $taskId);
        $targetIndex = $index === false ? null : $index + $direction;

        if ($index === false || $targetIndex === null || ! isset($siblings[$targetIndex])) {
            return;
        }

        $other = $siblings[$targetIndex];

        $order = $task->order;
        $task->update(['order' => $other->order]);
        $other->update(['order' => $order]);
    }

    /** @return Collection<int, Task> */
    private function siblingsOf(Task $task)
    {
        return $this->project->tasks()
            ->where('parent_id', $task->parent_id)
            ->orderBy('order')
            ->get();
    }

    /** @return array<string, mixed> */
    protected function rules(): array
    {
        return [
            'name' => 'required|string|max:255',
            'description' => 'nullable|string|max:2000',
            'startInput' => 'nullable|date',
            'duration' => 'required|integer|min:0|max:3650',
            'priority' => 'required|in:Low,Medium,High,Critical',
            'percentComplete' => 'required|integer|min:0|max:100',
            'parentId' => ['nullable', 'integer', 'max:3650', function (string $attribute, $value, callable $fail): void {
                if ($value === null || $this->editingId === null) {
                    return;
                }

                if ($value === $this->editingId) {
                    $fail(__('tasks.errors.parent_self'));

                    return;
                }

                $validator = app(DependencyValidator::class);

                if ($validator->isAncestorOf($this->editingId, $value, $this->project)) {
                    $fail(__('tasks.errors.parent_descendant'));

                    return;
                }

                if ($validator->depthOf($value, $this->project) + 1 >= 4) {
                    $fail(__('tasks.errors.parent_depth'));
                }
            }],
            'assignedResourceIds.*' => ['integer', 'exists:resources,id', function (string $attribute, $value, callable $fail): void {
                if ((int) $value === 0) {
                    return;
                }

                if (! Resource::query()->where('project_id', $this->project->id)->where('id', (int) $value)->exists()) {
                    $fail(__('tasks.errors.resource_foreign'));
                }
            }],
        ];
    }

    private function findTask(int $taskId): Task
    {
        return Task::query()
            ->where('project_id', $this->project->id)
            ->findOrFail($taskId);
    }

    private function resetForm(): void
    {
        $this->reset([
            'editingId',
            'name',
            'description',
            'startInput',
            'duration',
            'priority',
            'percentComplete',
            'parentId',
            'assignedResourceIds',
            'dependencyErrors',
        ]);

        $this->duration = 1;
        $this->priority = 'Medium';
        $this->percentComplete = 0;
        $this->newPredecessor = ['task_id' => null, 'type' => 'FS', 'lag' => 0];
    }

    /**
     * Keep the denormalised task_type in sync: Milestone (duration 0),
     * Parent (has children), Task (TSK-5 / display only).
     */
    private function syncTaskType(Task $task): void
    {
        $task->refresh();

        $type = match (true) {
            $task->children()->exists() => 'Parent',
            $task->duration === 0 => 'Milestone',
            default => 'Task',
        };

        if ($task->task_type !== $type) {
            $task->forceFill(['task_type' => $type])->saveQuietly();
        }
    }

    private function syncDescendantsTypes(Task $task): void
    {
        foreach ($task->children as $child) {
            $this->syncTaskType($child);
        }
    }

    public function render(): View
    {
        $tasks = $this->project->tasks()->orderBy('order')->get();
        $byParent = $tasks->groupBy('parent_id');

        $rows = [];
        $walk = function ($parentId, int $depth) use (&$walk, &$rows, $byParent): void {
            foreach ($byParent[$parentId] ?? [] as $task) {
                $rows[] = ['task' => $task, 'depth' => $depth];
                $walk($task->id, $depth + 1);
            }
        };
        $walk(null, 0);

        $assignments = Assignment::query()
            ->where('project_id', $this->project->id)
            ->with('resource:id,name')
            ->get()
            ->groupBy('task_id');

        // ASN-3: warn when an assigned member is on leave or double-booked.
        $warnings = [];
        foreach ($rows as $row) {
            $task = $row['task'];

            if ($task->effective_start === null || $task->effective_end === null) {
                continue;
            }

            foreach ($assignments[$task->id] ?? [] as $assignment) {
                $resource = $assignment->resource;

                if ($resource === null || $resource->trashed()) {
                    continue;
                }

                $onLeave = $resource->leaves()
                    ->where('start_date', '<=', $task->effective_end->format('Y-m-d'))
                    ->where('end_date', '>=', $task->effective_start->format('Y-m-d'))
                    ->exists();

                if ($onLeave) {
                    $warnings[$task->id][] = __('tasks.warning_leave', ['name' => $resource->name]);
                }

                $overlapping = Assignment::query()
                    ->where('resource_id', $resource->id)
                    ->where('task_id', '!=', $task->id)
                    ->whereHas('task', static function ($query) use ($task): void {
                        $query->where('effective_start', '<=', $task->effective_end->format('Y-m-d'))
                            ->where('effective_end', '>=', $task->effective_start->format('Y-m-d'));
                    })
                    ->exists();

                if ($overlapping) {
                    $warnings[$task->id][] = __('tasks.warning_overlap', ['name' => $resource->name]);
                }
            }
        }

        $memberFilter = $this->memberFilter;

        $filtered = $memberFilter === null
            ? $rows
            : array_values(array_filter($rows, static function (array $row) use ($assignments, $memberFilter): bool {
                $task = $row['task'];

                return ($assignments[$task->id] ?? null)?->contains(
                    static fn (Assignment $assignment): bool => $assignment->resource_id === $memberFilter
                ) ?? false;
            }));

        $predecessors = $this->editingId === null
            ? collect()
            : Dependency::query()
                ->where('project_id', $this->project->id)
                ->where('successor_id', $this->editingId)
                ->with('predecessor:id,name')
                ->get();

        // Predecessor candidates: every task except the one being edited.
        $predecessorCandidates = [];
        $walkCandidates = function ($parentId, int $depth) use (&$walkCandidates, &$predecessorCandidates, $byParent): void {
            foreach ($byParent[$parentId] ?? [] as $task) {
                $predecessorCandidates[] = ['task' => $task, 'depth' => $depth];
                $walkCandidates($task->id, $depth + 1);
            }
        };
        $walkCandidates(null, 0);

        return view('livewire.tasks.index', [
            'rows' => $filtered,
            'allTasks' => $tasks,
            'predecessorCandidates' => $predecessorCandidates,
            'resources' => $this->project->resources()->orderBy('name')->get(),
            'assignments' => $assignments,
            'warnings' => $warnings,
            'predecessors' => $predecessors,
            'parentCandidates' => $tasks
                ->whereNull('parent_id')
                ->reject(fn (Task $task): bool => $this->editingId !== null && $task->id === $this->editingId)
                ->values(),
        ]);
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Livewire\Gantt;

use App\Models\Assignment;
use App\Models\Dependency;
use App\Models\Holiday;
use App\Models\Project;
use App\Models\Resource;
use App\Models\Task;
use Carbon\CarbonImmutable;
use Illuminate\Contracts\View\View;
use Livewire\Attributes\Layout;
use Livewire\Component;

/**
 * GNT-1..GNT-4 (P0): task list + bars on a timeline, dependency arrows,
 * weekend/holiday shading, day/week/month zoom, distinct parent/milestone
 * shapes and a today line. CPM-2: critical bars are highlighted (red + thicker
 * border + ⚠ marker — not colour alone, PRD §9 accessibility).
 *
 * Only layout geometry is computed here — every date comes from the persisted
 * engine output (build rule; D-24).
 */
#[Layout('components.layouts.app')]
class Index extends Component
{
    public Project $project;

    public string $zoom = 'day';

    public ?int $memberFilter = null;

    private const ROW_HEIGHT = 28;

    private const HEADER_HEIGHT = 34;

    public function mount(Project $project): void
    {
        $this->project = $project;
    }

    public function render(): View
    {
        $tasks = $this->project->tasks()->orderBy('order')->get();
        $byParent = $tasks->groupBy('parent_id');

        $rows = [];
        $walk = function ($parentId, int $depth) use (&$walk, &$rows, $byParent): void {
            foreach ($byParent[$parentId] ?? [] as $task) {
                $rows[] = ['task' => $task, 'depth' => $depth];
                $walk($task->id, $depth + 1);
            }
        };
        $walk(null, 0);

        $assignments = Assignment::query()
            ->where('project_id', $this->project->id)
            ->with('resource:id,name')
            ->get();

        $memberFilter = $this->memberFilter;

        if ($memberFilter !== null) {
            $rows = array_values(array_filter(
                $rows,
                static fn (array $row): bool => $assignments
                    ->where('task_id', $row['task']->id)
                    ->contains('resource_id', $memberFilter),
            ));
        }

        $dated = $tasks->filter(static fn (Task $task): bool => $task->effective_start !== null && $task->effective_end !== null);

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Livewire\Projects;

use App\Models\Project;
use Illuminate\Contracts\View\View;
use Livewire\Attributes\Layout;
use Livewire\Attributes\Validate;
use Livewire\Component;

/**
 * PRJ-1 (create with name/organization/description) and PRJ-2 (list, open,
 * edit link, delete with confirmation).
 */
#[Layout('components.layouts.app')]
class Index extends Component
{
    #[Validate('required|string|max:255')]
    public string $name = '';

    #[Validate('nullable|string|max:255')]
    public string $organization = '';

    #[Validate('nullable|string|max:2000')]
    public string $description = '';

    public bool $showCreate = false;

    public ?int $deleteId = null;

    public function create(): void
    {
        $this->validate();

        $project = Project::create([
            'name' => $this->name,
            'organization' => $this->organization ?: null,
            'description' => $this->description ?: null,
        ]);

        $this->reset(['name', 'organization', 'description', 'showCreate']);

        $this->redirectRoute('projects.show', $project);
    }

    public function askDelete(int $projectId): void
    {
        $this->deleteId = $projectId;
    }

    public function cancelDelete(): void
    {
        $this->deleteId = null;
    }

    public function delete(): void
    {
        Project::findOrFail($this->deleteId)->delete();
        $this->deleteId = null;
    }

    public function render(): View
    {
        return view('livewire.projects.index', [
            'projects' => Project::query()->withCount(['tasks', 'resources'])->latest()->get(),
        ]);
    }
}

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Livewire\Projects;

use App\Models\Project;
use Illuminate\Contracts\View\View;
use Livewire\Attributes\Layout;

/**
 * PRJ-1 / PRJ-2: create and edit a project. Empty name is rejected with a
 * clear message (PRJ-1 AC).
 */
#[Layout('components.layouts.app')]
class Form extends Component
{
    public ?Project $project = null;

    #[Validate('required|string|max:255')]
    public string $name = '';

    #[Validate('nullable|string|max:255')]
    public string $organization = '';

    #[Validate('nullable|string|max:2000')]
    public string $description = '';

    public function mount(?Project $project = null): void
    {
        $this->project = $project;

        if ($project !== null) {
            $this->name = $project->name;
            $this->organization = (string) $project->organization;
            $this->description = (string) $project->description;
        }
    }

    public function save(): void
    {
        $this->validate();

        $data = [
            'name' => $this->name,
            'organization' => $this->organization ?: null,
            'description' => $this->description ?: null,
        ];

        if ($this->project === null) {
            $project = Project::create($data);
            $this->redirectRoute('projects.show', $project);

            return;
        }

        $this->project->update($data);

        $this->redirectRoute('projects.show', $this->project);
    }

    public function render(): View
    {
        return view('livewire.projects.form');
    }
}
